articles.title: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumors: Imaging Findings and a Multidisciplinary Approach to Treatment.
articles.abstract: Gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GISTs) have evolved from historically misclassified smooth muscle tumors to a distinct disease entity, defined by gain-of-function mutations in KIT or PDGFRA proto-oncogenes. The advent of targeted therapy for this entity in the form of a tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), imatinib mesylate, has transformed the treatment for GISTs, reducing recurrence and improving survival in patients with advanced disease. Radiologists play a critical role in initial lesion identification, surgical planning, and posttherapy surveillance, with cross-sectional imaging (CT and MRI) being vital in characterizing tumor features such as endophytic or exophytic nature, pseudocapsule, ulceration, necrosis, and changes in enhancement. Incorporating the Choi criteria into routine practice further refines response assessment, guiding adjustments in therapeutic strategy. A multidisciplinary approach is essential for optimal GIST management, requiring close collaboration between surgeons, oncologists, pathologists, and radiologists to establish a diagnosis, determine resectability, consider neoadjuvant or adjuvant TKIs, and monitor for disease recurrence (with imaging intervals tailored to risk classification). Future directions involve greater incorporation of molecular profiling to personalize treatments and the integration of newer-generation TKIs for imatinib-resistant cases, highlighting the continued importance of interdisciplinary coordination.

articles.title: Imaging in Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma).
articles.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) or scleroderma is a multisystem autoimmune disorder characterized by a variable pattern of skin thickening and involvement of visceral organs. The pathophysiology is similar across all organs, which is chronic low-grade inflammation, with vasculopathy and eventual fibrosis. Diagnosis is primarily clinical, particularly in patients with established disease comprising characteristic skin and visceral manifestations, with a supportive role of laboratory and imaging findings. The presence of radiologic signs such as hidebound bowel or a combination of patulous lower esophageal sphincter, pulmonary fibrosis, skin thickening, and Raynaud phenomenon is relatively specific for SSc. Nevertheless, imaging in SSc is primarily used to determine the pattern, severity, and complications of visceral organ involvement, rather than for diagnosis of SSc. Radiologic evaluation in SSc employs a wide gamut of investigations, depending on the organ of interest. For example, US is used for the skin and superficial tissues; fluoroscopy, CT, or MR enterography for the gastrointestinal tract; endoanal US or MRI for the internal anal sphincter; high-resolution CT for the lungs; echocardiography and cardiac MRI for SSc-related pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) and cardiac disease; and radiography, CT, or MRI for musculoskeletal involvement. Early diagnosis of treatable features, such as PAH and gastroesophageal reflux, can help reduce the morbidity and mortality associated with SSc. Imaging is additionally useful to prognosticate and monitor the disease. The authors focus on the multisystem, multimodality imaging manifestations of SSc with relevant differential diagnoses to bridge the gaps in knowledge about SSc. ©RSNA, 2026.

articles.title: Primary Amenorrhea: Diagnostic Approach, Imaging Spectrum, and Common Pitfalls.
articles.abstract: Primary amenorrhea is the absence of menarche in a 15-year-old adolescent girl who has developed secondary sex characteristics or a 13-year-old girl without development. Primary amenorrhea reflects disruption along the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian-uterine axis and may arise from a spectrum of anatomic, genetic, or functional abnormalities. Although primary amenorrhea is less common than secondary amenorrhea, recognition of the underlying level of dysfunction is essential for appropriate diagnosis and management as well as informed counseling regarding the patient's reproductive potential. A structured anatomic approach allows categorization of the causes into three levels based on the predominant site of dysfunction: level I, which involves the uterus and vaginal outflow tract; level II, which involves the ovaries and gonads; and level III, which involves the hypothalamus and pituitary gland. This classification system emphasizes a systematic and multidisciplinary approach to diagnosis and treatment, integrating clinical and biochemical testing and targeted imaging to localize the underlying dysfunction and guide treatment. Transabdominal US serves as the first-line imaging modality to help determine the presence and morphology of the pelvic organs. MRI provides detailed characterization of müllerian and urinary tract anomalies and allows evaluation of the hypothalamic-pituitary region when central causes are suspected.

articles.title: Segmental FLIS and ANALI provide complementary MR-based risk stratification in primary sclerosing cholangitis.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To assess the reproducibility of a segmental functional liver imaging score (S-FLIS) and whether it improves risk stratification in primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) beyond global FLIS (G-FLIS) and established MRI/MRCP-based scores (ANALI, ANALI Gd+, DiStrict), alone or combined. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This prospective study included consecutive adult PSC patients undergoing standardised gadoxetic acid-enhanced MRI, blood tests and liver stiffness measurement (LSM). G-FLIS, S-FLIS, DiStrict, ANALI and ANALI Gd+ were computed, and interobserver agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa. Univariate and bivariate logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses evaluated discrimination for two surrogate risk biomarkers: LSM > 9.6 kPa and Mayo risk score (MRS) > 0. RESULTS: Seventy-seven patients were included (median age 45 years; 62.3% male). Interobserver agreement was almost perfect for DiStrict (κ = 0.98), substantial for G-FLIS (κ = 0.608) and moderate to almost perfect for S-FLIS across hepatic segments (κ = 0.524-0.861). Unlike G-FLIS, S-FLIS was significantly associated with both high LSM and high MRS. Among individual scores, S-FLIS achieved the highest discriminative performance for high LSM (AUC = 0.782) and high MRS (AUC = 0.816), outperforming ANALI (0.668 and 0.702) and DiStrict (0.713 and 0.741). Bivariate models combining ANALI and S-FLIS achieved the highest performance for both endpoints (AUC = 0.843 and 0.864). CONCLUSION: S-FLIS outperformed established morphological MRI/MRCP scores in identifying high-risk PSC patients, and pairing functional (S-FLIS) with morphological (ANALI) assessment yielded the greatest incremental value, supporting a multiparametric non-invasive approach to risk stratification in PSC. KEY POINTS: Question Can an S-FLIS improve non-invasive risk stratification in PSC beyond whole-liver FLIS and established morphological MRI/MRCP scores, alone or in combination? Findings S-FLIS outperformed FLIS, ANALI, and DiStrict as a standalone discriminator of high-risk PSC patients, and its combination with ANALI achieved the highest discriminative accuracy (AUC up to 0.864). Clinical relevance S-FLIS is a reproducible, non-invasive MRI biomarker of hepatocellular function in PSC; combined with the morphological ANALI score, it may enhance non-invasive risk stratification, pending validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

articles.title: Respiratory-compensated non-contrast vs breath-hold contrast-enhanced MR angiography in pediatric Fontan patients.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare a highly accelerated ECG-triggered and navigator-gated, non-contrast respiratory-compensated 3D magnetic resonance angiography with Dixon water-fat separation (NC-MRA) to respiratory-suspended non-ECG-triggered multiphase contrast-enhanced MRA (CE-MRA) in pediatric patients with partial or total cavopulmonary connection (PCPC/TCPC). MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, between 02/2021 and 09/2023, 30 consecutive pediatric patients (mean age 3.6 ± 0.8 years) with PCPC or TCPC underwent 1.5 T cardiovascular MRI under deep sedation and mechanical ventilation. NC-MRA was acquired before contrast administration alongside standard CE-MRA. Two blinded readers independently evaluated image quality using a 5-point Likert scale and measured vascular diameters of predefined aortic segments, the Glenn anastomosis, Fontan conduit, and pulmonary arteries in consensus. Datasets were presented in randomized order. We used paired statistical testing for method comparison and Cohen's kappa to assess inter-rater agreement. RESULTS: Mean NC-MRA acquisition time (5:55 ± 2:19 min) was comparable to that of multiphase CE-MRA (5:48 ± 3:03 min), including pre-contrast acquisition p = 0.54). Overall image quality was generally comparable between techniques for most vascular segments (NC-MRA median 5, IQR 5-5, CE-MRA median 5, IQR 4-5, p = 0.06-0.52). No significant differences were found in vascular diameter measurements across all segments (p = 0.06-0.59). Inter-reader agreement was at least substantial (κ > 0.65). CONCLUSION: Respiratory-compensated NC-MRA at 1.5 T provides image quality and vascular diameter measurements comparable to CE-MRA in pediatric PCPC/TCPC patients. Eliminating breath-holds and contrast administration, the technique simplifies workflow, avoids mechanical ventilation, and improves patient safety in this vulnerable population. KEY POINTS: Question Is a non-contrast, ECG-triggered, and navigator-gated 3D MRA sequence diagnostically equivalent to conventional breath-hold CE-MRA for vascular assessment in pediatric Fontan patients? Findings There were no significant differences in vascular diameters, and image quality was comparable between both sequences in most segments, showing substantial inter-rater agreement and diagnostic reliability. Clinical relevance Non-contrast, ECG-triggered, and navigator-gated MRA enables reliable vascular assessment in pediatric Fontan patients without gadolinium or breath-holds, reducing anesthesia requirements, improving safety, and simplifying workflow in this vulnerable population.

articles.title: Appropriate Use Criteria for 18F-Floretyrosine (FET) PET Imaging in Patients with Primary Brain Tumors.
Total-Body 18F-FAPI PET/CT for Assessment of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Pilot Study.
articles.abstract: Liver biopsy remains the gold standard for fibrosis assessment; however, its invasiveness limits its suitability for routine clinical use. The rising prevalence of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) as a leading cause of chronic liver disease and hepatocellular carcinoma underscores the need for reliable noninvasive assessment. Current noninvasive imaging methods provide surrogate measures of fibrosis but do not directly assess fibrogenic activity. In contrast, fibroblast activation protein inhibitor (FAPI) PET enables molecular imaging of activated fibroblasts, a key driver of fibrosis. This study evaluates dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET imaging to assess hepatic fibrogenic activity in MASLD. Methods: In this prospective pilot study, 10 subjects (3 healthy volunteers, 4 patients with mild-moderate fibrosis, and 3 patients with advanced fibrosis) underwent 60-min dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET/CT. SUV and blood-normalized SUV ratio (SUVR) were quantified across time frames, and the net influx rate was derived from dynamic data. MR elastography-derived liver stiffness values were obtained for comparison. Correlations with histologic fibrosis scoring of biopsy tissue were assessed using Spearman analysis. Results: At 5 min postinjection, SUVR correlated strongly with histologic fibrosis score (ρ = 0.95; 95% CI, 0.75-1.00; P = 1.89 × 10-5), followed by SUV (ρ = 0.78; 95% CI, 0.23-0.98; P = 0.0077) and net influx rate from kinetic modeling (ρ = 0.84; 95% CI, 0.41-0.98; P = 0.0022). SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval allowed clearer differentiation among healthy volunteers, patients with mild fibrosis, and patients with advanced fibrosis. Conclusion: Dynamic 18F-FAPI-74 PET enables quantitative visualization of hepatic fibroblast activation in MASLD. SUVR at the 4- to 5-min interval correlates more strongly with fibrosis severity, supporting 18F-FAPI-74 PET as a promising molecular biomarker for assessing and potentially monitoring metabolic fibrosis.

articles.title: Comparable Daughter Radionuclide Redistribution with Superior Tumor Absorbed Dose of the SSTR2 Antagonist [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 Versus [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE.
articles.abstract: It has been hypothesized that effective cellular internalization is required for the retention of 225Ac daughter radionuclides. Both the complex decay chain of 225Ac and the recoil-mediated release of daughters, particularly 213Bi (half-life, 46 min), raise concerns about redistribution that may reduce tumor absorbed dose (TAD) and increase off-target radiation exposure. Because somatostatin receptor subtype 2 antagonists, such as satoreotide tetraxetan (SSO110, also known as DOTA-JR11), are not internalized, it has been proposed that the daughter radionuclides are less effectively retained compared with internalizing agonists, such as DOTATATE. In this study, we performed a direct and quantitative comparison of daughter radionuclide redistribution after administration of [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 and [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Methods: Biodistribution and 213Bi redistribution were evaluated in BALB/c nude mice bearing NCI-H69 small cell lung cancer xenografts. Repeated γ-counting combined with biexponential modeling was used to quantify 225Ac and 213Bi activity in tumors, blood, bone marrow, kidneys, the liver, and the intestines up to 96 h postinjection. TAD was calculated with and without accounting for experimentally derived 213Bi redistribution. Real-time in vitro binding assays were conducted to characterize cellular retention of [225Ac]Ac-SSO110. Results: [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 demonstrated higher tumor uptake and prolonged retention compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution of 213Bi from tumors was minimal and comparable between the agonist and antagonist and reduced the TAD by 4.5% for [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 and 3.9% for [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. After accounting for this redistribution, [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 delivered a 2.8-fold higher TAD and a 1.8-fold higher tumor-to-kidney absorbed dose (AD) ratio compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Moreover, 213Bi redistribution had no relevant impact on AD estimates in evaluated healthy organs, including the kidneys, the intestines, blood, and bone marrow. Real-time binding studies demonstrated a sustained cell-associated β--signal after incubation with [225Ac]Ac-SSO110. Conclusion: Despite negligible internalization, [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 did not show increased macroscopic 213Bi redistribution compared with the internalizing agonist [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Redistribution was limited for both radiopeptides and had only a minor effect on AD estimates for tumors and the evaluated healthy tissues. [225Ac]Ac-SSO110 achieved a higher TAD and more favorable tumor-to-kidney ratio compared with [225Ac]Ac-DOTATATE. Overall, these findings support further evaluation of antagonist-based 225Ac radiopharmaceutical therapy.

articles.title: A SPECT-Guided, PET-Sparing Algorithm for PSMA Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Evaluation (SPARE).
articles.abstract: [177Lu]Lu-PSMA radiopharmaceutical therapy is delivered as repeated cycles, yet the decision to continue or adapt treatment after the second cycle is not standardized. Posttherapy SPECT/CT is routinely performed but rarely used formally for response assessment. We developed a multimodality, response-adapted algorithm applied after cycle 2 and tested its concordance with real-world decisions. Methods: We studied 142 men with metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer (formerly metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer) who completed at least 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA and underwent posttherapy SPECT/CT, baseline and 12-wk prostate-specific antigen (PSA) testing, and baseline and interim prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET and [18F]FDG PET. Response was assessed in accordance with Prostate Cancer Working Group 4 recommendations for PSA and with RECIP 1.0 for SPECT and PSMA PET. The algorithm combined SPECT/CT and PSA, used PSMA PET only when both were stable, and yielded 3 recommendations: continue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, discontinue [177Lu]Lu-PSMA, or consider [18F]FDG PET. The primary endpoints were the number of interim PSMA PET studies avoided and the concordance between algorithm recommendations (continue vs. discontinue) and real-world decisions. The secondary endpoint was intermodality response evaluation concordance. Results: The algorithm recommended continuation in 74 patients (52.1%), discontinuation in 49 patients (34.5%), and [18F]FDG PET in 19 patients (13.4%). Interim PSMA PET/CT could be avoided in 120 patients (84.5%) (95% CI, 77.7%-89.5%). Among patients with a definitive recommendation, conditional agreement of the algorithm with real-world management decisions was 91.1% (95% CI, 84.7%-94.9%), with a κ of 0.81 (95% CI, 0.69-0.91). All 74 patients (100%) with an algorithm recommendation to continue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment continuation, whereas 38 (78%) of 49 patients with an algorithm recommendation to discontinue treatment had matching real-world decisions for treatment discontinuation. Response classification on SPECT agreed only moderately with PSA level (κ = 0.45) and PSMA PET (κ = 0.47), but the combination of SPECT and PSA raised agreement with PSMA PET to "substantial" (κ = 0.67), approaching that of PSMA PET with PSA level (κ = 0.70). Every discordant decision (n = 11) occurred when the algorithm recommended treatment discontinuation in a patient who nonetheless continued treatment, most commonly because [177Lu]Lu-PSMA was being used as a last line of therapy (7/11, 64%). Conclusion: A SPECT-guided algorithm could have avoided most interim PSMA PET studies and reproduced real-world treatment decisions after 2 cycles of [177Lu]Lu-PSMA with high agreement. This algorithm may serve as the basis for a standardized treatment management framework, pending independent, prospective outcome-based validation.

articles.title: PSMA Total Tumor Volume: A Simple Quantifiable Biomarker for Overall Survival Prediction-Results from the International PROMISE PET Registry.
articles.abstract: Prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET is an accurate prognostic imaging biomarker of survival in patients with prostate cancer when assessed using Prostate Cancer Molecular Imaging Standardized Evaluation (PROMISE) criteria. Previously, PSMA PET PROMISE risk nomograms were created that surpassed clinical prediction tools. In this study, we focused on the evaluation of quantifiable biomarkers to simplify and facilitate overall survival (OS) prediction. Methods: Data from patients with histologically proven prostate cancer who underwent PSMA PET between December 2012 and April 2024 at participating imaging centers worldwide and who were included in the PROMISE PET Registry by January 31, 2026, were analyzed. Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels at PSMA PET, disease stage, and OS follow-up data were collected. PSMA total tumor volume (PSMA TTV) and whole-body SUVmean were assessed using predefined SUV thresholds. PSMA total lesion uptake (PSMA TL) was calculated as PSMA TTV × SUVmean PSA level at PSMA PET adjusted for PSMA TTV was calculated as PSA × TTV. Univariate regression analysis was conducted to identify potential predictors. Prognostic accuracy of quantitative biomarkers was compared using Harrell C-indices and time-dependent concordance in the development cohort. Probabilities for 3-, 5-, and 7-y OS across PSMA TTV quartiles were derived from Kaplan-Meier curves. Subgroup analysis was conducted by cancer stage. Results: In total, 13,893 patients were included in the analysis and divided 2:1 into development (n = 9271) and validation (n = 4622) cohorts. The prognostic accuracy of PSMA TTV in the validation cohort (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.77-0.80) was superior to SUVmean (C-index, 0.62; 95% CI, 0.61-0.64) and PSA level at PET (C-index, 0.71; 95% CI, 0.69-0.72) and similar to PSMA TL (C-index, 0.78; 95% CI, 0.76-0.79) and PSA × TTV (C-index, 0.77; 95% CI, 0.75-0.78). In the entire cohort, the median OS for PSMA TTV quartile 1 (0 mL) and quartile 2 (>0-2.1 mL) was not reached. The median OS was 11.4 y (interquartile range, 10.1 y to not reached) for PSMA TTV quartile 3 (>2.1-16.2 mL) and 4.4 y (interquartile range, 4.2-4.6 y) for quartile 4 (>16.17 mL). Conclusion: Among quantifiable PET metrics, PSMA TTV had the highest prognostic accuracy for OS in patients with prostate cancer. Automated PSMA TTV assessment may facilitate fast and reproducible outcome prediction in the future.

articles.title: 2026 SNMMI Highlights Lecture: Oncology and Therapy.
articles.abstract: The Highlights Lecture, presented at the closing session of each SNMMI Annual Meeting, was originated and presented for more than 30 y by Henry N. Wagner, Jr., MD. Beginning in 2010, the duties of summarizing selected significant presentations at the meeting were divided annually among 4 distinguished nuclear and molecular medicine subject matter experts. The 2026 Highlights Lectures were delivered on June 2, 2026 at the SNMMI Annual Meeting in Los Angeles, California. Presented here is the lecture by David M. Schuster, MD, FACR, Emory University Hospital in Atlanta, Georgia, who spoke on oncology and therapy topics presented at the meeting. Note that in the following presentation summary, numerals in brackets represent abstract numbers as published in The Journal of Nuclear Medicine (2026;67[suppl 1]).

articles.title: Test-Retest Repeatability of Peripheral Ganglion Uptake on 18F-DCFPyL PET/CT: Implications for Interpreting Benign Uptake on PSMA PET.
articles.abstract: Repeatability of uptake in benign structures on prostate-specific membrane antigen PET is unexplored and poorly understood. We used a post hoc analysis of a test-retest cohort to assess repeatability of uptake in peripheral ganglia. Methods: Twenty-two patients were included. Spheric volumes of interest were manually placed on the cervical and lumbosacral dorsal root ganglia, the cervicothoracic ganglia, and the celiac ganglia. Repeatability was quantified using intraclass correlation coefficient, within-subject coefficient of variation, and Bland-Altman limits of agreement. Results: Ganglion uptake demonstrated an intraclass correlation coefficient of 0.82 and a within-subject coefficient of variation of 13.1%. Bland-Altman analysis on a relative scale demonstrated that the mean bias was 0.9%, with 95% limits of agreement ranging from -35.8% to 37.6%, broadly comparable to the repeatability of prostate cancer tumors previously reported. Conclusion: The repeatability of uptake in peripheral ganglia on prostate-specific membrane antigen PET scans is similar to the repeatability of uptake in prostate cancer tumors. As such, isolated changes in uptake cannot be used as de facto evidence of a malignant lesion.

articles.title: From Nobel-Winning Science to Real-World Impact: Carolyn Bertozzi Talks with Ken Herrmann on Discovery, Entrepreneurship, and Leadership.
Science, Mentorship, and Total-Body PET: A Conversation Between Simon Cherry and Johannes Czernin.
Donor Site Evaluation Using Multispectral Optoacoustic Tomography in Patients with Head and Neck Cancer Who Require Free Flap Transplant Surgery.
articles.abstract: Head and neck cancer surgery requires autologous tissue transplants to reconstruct resection defects. The outcome of reconstructive surgery is often limited by perfusion-associated complications. To improve patient outcome, innovative approaches to detect perfusion deficits are essential for selecting the optimal free flap transplant donor site. Methods: A clinical pilot study was conducted that included 16 patients with head and neck cancer who were undergoing surgery and 10 healthy controls. Multispectral optoacoustic tomography (MSOT) was performed before surgery at the most common donor sites (radial forearm, latissimus dorsi, anterolateral thigh, and distal fibula). The biomarker of oxygen saturation in muscle and in the dermal layer was compared between healthy controls and patients and was correlated with clinical postsurgical outcomes. Results: MSOT examinations caused no adverse reactions and integrated smoothly into the clinical workflow. MSOT-derived muscle oxygen saturation showed significant differences between patients and healthy controls at all donor sites. These disparities became more pronounced under muscle provocation, revealing perfusion deficits that were previously not detected. Furthermore, exercise revealed side-to-side differences in hemoglobin saturation that exceeded 20%. Patients experiencing postoperative complications exhibited substantially reduced preoperative perfusion levels. Conclusion: In this clinical study, we demonstrated the feasibility of MSOT for donor site evaluation in autologous transplant surgery. Our findings highlight the potential of MSOT-derived hemoglobin metrics as functional imaging biomarkers for detection of perfusion deficits.

articles.title: Prostate-Specific Membrane Antigen PET/CT Segmentation Guided by Vision Language Models Embedding Clinical Report Semantics.
articles.abstract: Whole-body prostate-specific membrane antigen (PSMA) PET/CT segmentation remains challenging: manual contouring is unsustainable, and image-only artificial intelligence models often misclassify physiologic uptake as malignant, causing high false-positive rates. These limitations underscore the need for segmentation strategies that incorporate the nuclear medicine expertise encoded in PET/CT reports but not used by current models. We investigated whether routine PET/CT reports improve automated lesion segmentation for prostate cancer. Methods: We developed a language-guided 3-dimensional SegResNet fusing report text with 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT image features, encoding report semantics via 4 strategies (BiomedVLP, RadGraph, GPT-raw, GPT-engineered) compared with an image-only model (baseline). Of 320 patients who underwent 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT, 297 studies were available; 13 were excluded for missing reports or incomplete image-mask pairs, leaving 284 for analysis, split at the patient level into 243 development cases and a fixed 41-case held-out test set. Metrics included Dice, intersection over union (IoU), precision, recall, average symmetric surface distance, 95th percentile Hausdorff distance, surface Dice similarity at 5 mm, and lesion-level false positives, using 3 matching criteria (any overlap; 1-to-1 maximum IoU matching, IoU ≥ 0.5; and correct localization of the SUVmax voxel). Significance was assessed using paired 1-sided Wilcoxon tests with Holm adjustment. Results: Report guidance consistently reduced false positives and improved whole-mask boundary agreement. False-positive lesions were reduced by nearly 4 per patient with BiomedVLP and by approximately 3 per patient with RadGraph and GPT-raw. Average symmetric surface distance decreased from 105.4 ± 62.5 mm (image only) to 23.4 ± 18.2 mm with BiomedVLP, 36.9 ± 22.4 mm with RadGraph, and 36.3 ± 26.4 mm with GPT-raw; 95th percentile Hausdorff distance improved from 455.0 ± 169.3 mm to 123.8 ± 80.3 mm with BiomedVLP, and surface Dice similarity at 5 mm increased from 0.638 ± 0.172 to 0.705 ± 0.181. However, when these surface metrics were recomputed on matched true-positive lesions only using the same 3 criteria, no language-guided model differed significantly from the image-only model for any surface metric (all Holm-adjusted P = 1.0), indicating that the whole-mask improvements were attributable to false-positive suppression rather than genuine gains in contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. Precision increased for BiomedVLP (0.099) and RadGraph (0.060), with a modest decrease in voxel-level recall (-0.051, BiomedVLP), reflecting a precision-recall trade-off from suppression of spurious uptake. Dice improved by 0.032 but was borderline significant; IoU increased for BiomedVLP (0.036). Lesion-level sensitivity changed by no more than 0.04 for all models and did not reach significance. Total lesion PSMA remained highly correlated with manual measurements (r ≥ 0.85), whereas PSMA tumor volume correlations were more variable across models (r = 0.37-0.70). Conclusion: The integration of PET/CT report semantics into automated PSMA PET/CT segmentation substantially reduced false-positive lesions and preserved total lesion PSMA agreement with manual measurements; a matched true-positive-only reanalysis indicated that the accompanying whole-mask boundary-agreement gains reflected false-positive suppression rather than improved contour accuracy on correctly detected lesions. This approach may reduce manual cleanup and support more reliable quantitative workflows, although precision gains should be weighed against a modest recall reduction. External validation, extension of the true-positive-only analysis to independent cohorts, and PSMA-specific language pretraining are warranted.

articles.title: Medicare beneficiaries have less follow-up imaging and more invasive procedures than NLST participants following lung screening.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To determine if the proportion of patients receiving thoracic imaging, invasive diagnostic, or surgical procedures following community lung cancer screening (LCS) differed from that in the National Lung Screening Trial (NLST). METHODS: We compared the proportion of NLST participants and 2018 Medicare beneficiaries receiving imaging, invasive, or surgical procedures in the six months and one year following LCS, as well as lung cancer incidence and all-cause mortality. To create comparable cohorts, we used NLST chart abstraction data to impute information on procedures for participants with no abstraction. RESULTS: Within six months and one-year of LCS, NLST participants were significantly more likely to have at least one imaging test than Medicare beneficiaries (21.4 versus 16.5%); (difference=4.97%; 95% confidence limits (CL) 1.85%, 8.09) and 26.6% versus 22.3% (difference=4.28; 95% CL: 0.55, 8.02) respectively. NLST participants were significantly less likely to have an invasive or surgical procedure within six months of LCS (0.60 versus 4.64%; difference: -4.04% ; 95% CL: -5.23%, -2.84%) and (0.28 versus 1.51%; difference: -1.22% ; 95% CL: -1.80%, -0.65%) respectively, but neither differed significantly at one year. NLST had more cases of lung cancer diagnosed (3.83% [95% CL: 3.33,4.33] versus Medicare 2.26% [95%CL:1.51,3.01]). Mortality was not significantly different. CONCLUSIONS: Medicare beneficiaries were less likely to have follow-up imaging within six months and one year of LCS, and they were more likely to undergo invasive diagnostic or surgical procedures at six months, but were not statistically significant at one year following LCS.

articles.title: Closing the Loop on Incidental Intracranial Aneurysms: An AI-Assisted Patient Navigation Program Deployed Across a Large Health System.
Depth-compensated regularization for volumetric inverse electrocardiography.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Accurate non-invasive localization of Premature Ventricular Contractions (PVCs) is critical for guiding catheter ablation, yet the standard inverse Electrocardiographic Imaging (ECGI) problem suffers from an inherent depth-bias that misprojects deep intramural sources onto the epicardial surface. METHODS: We propose a volumetric estimation of transmembrane potentials by means of a convex optimization functional that integrates depth-compensating weights, derived from the resolution matrix of the forward operator, into both a weighted Lasso (ℓ1) penalty and a weighted Anisotropic Total Variation regularizer, with truncation stabilized by Generalized Cross-Validation. The framework is validated on 625 PVC simulations uniformly distributed throughout a biventricular myocardium, and its applicability is demonstrated on a clinical recording from a public repository comprising 21 catheter-referenced pacing sites. RESULTS: The Weighted Lasso+Weighted TV formulation achieved a median Correlation Coefficient of 0.79 and a median Geodesic Localization Error of 6.98 mm, compared to 0.22 and 35.29 mm, respectively, for the unweighted Lasso baseline. Compared to the unweighted Lasso+TV, the inclusion of depth-compensating weights maintained comparable performance on epicardial sources while reducing the standard deviation of the Geodesic Localization Error from 28.73 mm to 4.92 mm and from 27.48 mm to 4.36 mm for myocardial and endocardial origins, respectively. On the clinical recording, the median Geodesic Localization Error of the unweighted formulation increased from 27.6 mm at non-septal pacing sites to 65.6 mm at septal ones, whereas the depth-compensated formulation remained comparable across both groups, 22.8 and 25.8 mm. CONCLUSION: Depth-compensated weighted regularization effectively mitigates epicardial bias in volumetric ECGI, providing a robust framework for non-invasive PVC localization without degrading superficial accuracy. Its applicability is demonstrated on a clinical recording, where the same attenuation of the depth-related bias is observed.

articles.title: OSS: Open suturing skills vision-based assessment challenge 2024-2025.
articles.abstract: Achieving high levels of surgical skill through effective training is essential for optimal patient outcomes. Automated, data-driven skill assessment holds significant potential to improve surgical training. While machine learning-based methods are increasingly popular for assessing skills in minimally invasive surgery, their application to open surgery remains limited. We present the results of a dedicated MICCAI challenge designed to benchmark and advance vision-based skill assessment in open surgery. The challenge dataset comprises videos of an open suturing training task recorded with a static GoPro camera in a dry-lab setting, with instrument trajectories available in addition to the primary video modality. The OSS Challenge was hosted over two consecutive years, comprising two and three independent tasks, respectively: (1) classifying skill level into four classes, (2) predicting the full Objective Structured Assessment of Technical Skills across eight categories, and (3) tracking hands and surgical tools. Participants submitted diverse solutions including deep learning-based video models, tracking-driven methods, and hybrid approaches. General-purpose spatiotemporal video models consistently achieved the strongest performance, though conceptually diverse approaches reached competitive levels when well-executed. Predicting fine-grained OSATS scores remains challenging but benefits substantially from increased training data. Keypoint tracking proves difficult given frequent occlusions and out-of-frame instances, limiting current applicability for motion-based skill analysis. This work benchmarks innovative and diverse solutions for surgical skill assessment, highlighting both the promise and current limitations of video-based evaluation in open surgery and identifying critical directions for advancing automated skill assessment toward clinical impact.

articles.title: Joint-embedding self-supervised representation learning for robust cone-beam CT segmentation.
articles.abstract: Cone-beam CT (CBCT) segmentation is challenged by reconstruction artifacts and limited reliable annotations. We investigate joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA)-style self-supervised learning for volumetric CBCT segmentation using CBCT-LGR, which extends our preliminary slice-wise conference study through fully three-dimensional local-global encoding, learnable semantic tokens, and a combined objective comprising local-global alignment, semantic alignment, and predictive consistency. We compare CBCT-LGR with supervised baselines (nnU-Net and STU-Net), generic self-supervised methods (BYOL-Med3D and Models Genesis), and foundation models (SAM, MedSAM, and Anatomix) using harmonized patient-level splits, preprocessing, and evaluation metrics while retaining each method's stated supervision setting. For representation-learning methods, frozen encoders are evaluated using supervised decoders trained with the same 10-subject labeled-data budget per dataset. Across three datasets, CBCT-LGR outperforms the generic self-supervised baselines on dataset-average overlap and boundary metrics. On CBCTLiTS, supervised and fine-tuned foundation-model approaches achieve higher absolute DSC under clean reconstruction conditions. Across five controlled reconstruction-quality levels, however, CBCT-LGR exhibits the smallest maximum relative DSC decline among all nine methods, with declines of 1.5% for liver and 14.5% for tumor, and achieves the highest numerical tumor DSC at the two most degraded levels. Results on Dataset 1 quantify agreement with imperfect reference annotations and do not establish true anatomical accuracy or a definitive method ranking. These findings define the capabilities and limitations of JEPA-style pretraining for volumetric CBCT segmentation.

articles.title: Hierarchical causal construction for semantic-granularity-aligned counterfactual medical image generation.
articles.abstract: Counterfactual image generation seeks to answer how a medical image should change when a clinical semantic factor is altered, and is important for model interpretation, lesion localization, and controllable image editing. This work addresses the semantic granularity mismatch in existing counterfactual generation methods and formulates it as the problem of semantic-granularity alignment (SGA). Specifically, counterfactual queries typically target macro-level semantics, such as lesion morphology, tissue intensity, or risk phenotype, whereas generative models operate on micro-level visual units, including pixels, patches, textures, and local boundaries. Without an explicit correspondence between these two levels, macro-level semantic interventions cannot be reliably translated into changes in the relevant local structures. To address this issue, we propose hierarchical causal construction (HCC), which uses causal abstraction to establish a hierarchical mapping between micro-level visual units and macro-level clinical semantics. We further integrate HCC with causal representation learning (CRL) to develop HCC-CRL, which first encodes an image into micro-level causal nodes, and then aggregates them into macro-level causal nodes and semantic slots through a learnable soft quotient mapping. Counterfactual interventions are subsequently performed at the macro level, and the intervened states are projected back into the micro-level visual space for counterfactual image generation. Within a unified hierarchical causal representation, the framework jointly models target semantic changes, preservation of non-target information, and local visual consistency. Experiments on Morpho-MNIST, the Breast Ultrasound Images (BUSI) dataset, and a microvascular invasion (MVI) prediction task show that HCC-CRL generates counterfactual images with well-directed semantic changes and improved structural preservation, while maintaining a robust balance among intervention success, identity preservation, and image quality.

articles.title: SurgPace: Complexity-aware progressive distillation for surgical multimodal large language models.
articles.abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have shown strong potential in robotic surgery for question answering, scene understanding, and grounded assistance, but their high computational cost limits real clinical deployment. Knowledge distillation provides a practical way to build compact surgical MLLMs, yet direct distillation is not well suited to surgical data because surgical samples vary greatly in difficulty, visual ambiguity, and required clinical context, making uniform teacher-student transfer unstable. In addition, the role of supervision changes during training: early stages require stronger teacher guidance for multimodal alignment, while later stages rely more on task supervision for effective optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SurgPace, a complexity-aware continuous curriculum framework for progressive distillation of surgical vision-language models. SurgPace estimates sample complexity using predictive confidence and Lorentz geometric consistency, and uses the fused score to guide a continuous easy-to-hard training process. We further introduce hierarchical representation alignment, which aligns the student with the teacher at the feature, logit, and probability levels, while gradually shifting the training focus from teacher imitation to task supervision. This design separates sample-level curriculum from objective-level scheduling, leading to more stable and effective distillation. We evaluate SurgPace on Surg-396 K, a benchmark built from four public surgical datasets and covering five dialogue paradigms. SurgPace consistently outperforms strong MLLM distillation baselines, demonstrating its effectiveness for building compact, memory-efficient surgical MLLMs with faster decoding under controlled benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/hezhicheng2002/SurgPace.

articles.title: CPCLNet: Advancing Cross-Modal Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation with Clustering-Inspired Prototype Consistency Learning.
articles.abstract: Cross-modal few-shot medical image segmentation (FSMIS) provides a solution for alleviating annotation scarcity and improving generalization across imaging modalities. However, severe modality discrepancy can disrupt support-query matching, contaminate support-derived foreground and background prototypes, and produce noisy affinity maps, making target-modality segmentation unreliable. To address this problem, we propose CPCLNet, a clustering-inspired prototype consistency learning network for cross-modal FSMIS. CPCLNet formulates cross-modal segmentation as a prototype consistency learning problem and progressively improves feature-space consistency, prototype reliability, and affinity-map coherence. Specifically, a parameter-sharing feature encoder provides a common representation basis across modalities, and a cross-modal distribution alignment module performs episode-specific support-query alignment. A clustering-inspired representative prototype descriptor further suppresses unstable support responses and constructs compact, modality-robust prototypes. Finally, an RWKV-based affinity map prediction module propagates prototype-guided correspondence across long-range spatial contexts with linear complexity. Extensive experiments on three imaging modalities, demonstrate that CPCLNet outperforms existing methods, achieving an average Dice improvement of 3.34 percentage points over the second-best competitor across CT→MRI and CT→PET tasks under both 1-shot and 5-shot settings. Further integration with MedSAM yields consistent improvements, indicating CP-CLNet's complementary potential with foundation models.

articles.title: Clinical-SAM: Agentic Test-Time Adaptation of SAM via Physician-in-the-Loop for Clinical Tumor Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Interactive foundation models such as SAM struggle to generalize across clinical deployment sites. Among existing adaptation strategies, test-time adaptation (TTA) is the most promising, yet current TTA methods trade one problem for another: removing the physician eliminates clinical grounding, while retaining the physician reintroduces a costly annotation burden. In this work, we propose Clinical-SAM, a two-phase agentic physician-in-the-loop TTA framework that teaches a frozen SAM to approximate what a physician would accept - directly and continuously, without requiring spatial annotations. In Phase I (pre-deployment), a self-prompting agent trained via reinforcement learning generates prompts autonomously, eliminating per-case expert spatial input at inference. In Phase II (deployment), the agent policy is refined online by the one signal physicians already produce: a binary accept/reject feedback on each proposed mask. As the binary feedback accumulates across deployed cases, the agent converges toward a policy that produces masks meeting a reference acceptance standard designed to approximate physician judgment, with progressively fewer interactions. We evaluate Clinical-SAM in a pre-clinical setting on six oncological benchmarks spanning CT (colon, pancreas, liver, kidney) and PET (head & neck, lung) tumor segmentation, using agreement with reference-standard segmentations as a proxy for physician acceptance. Clinical-SAM achieves state-of-the-art performance on all six datasets, outperforming fine-tuning, interactive, TTA, and online-learning baselines, while requiring only 3.3 binary judgments per case on average across the six datasets. Our code is available here.

articles.title: Unafraid: Reflections From a Medical Student Entering Radiology in the Face of Warnings About Artificial Intelligence.
(Elastography) E-BI-RADS: A Novel Classification System for Breast Elastography to Enable Safe Biopsy De-escalation.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Determining the probability of malignancy of a breast lesion allows for the appropriate triage of follow-up. Although BI-RADS provides standardized risk stratification for mammography, ultrasound, and magnetic resonance imaging, no equivalent classification system exists for breast elastography. The aim of this study was to develop and evaluate a data-driven E-BI-RADS classification for breast elastography and to compare its diagnostic performance with B-mode BI-RADS. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this retrospective study, consecutive patients undergoing breast imaging with available B-mode ultrasound, shear-wave elastography (SWE), and strain elastography (10L4 transducer, Siemens ACUSON Sequoia) from 06/2023 to 12/2025 were included. A multivariable logistic regression model combining SWE velocity and elastography-to-B-mode lesion size (E/B) ratio was used to estimate malignancy probability, followed by Platt recalibration. Data-driven probability cutoffs were derived to define E-BI-RADS categories aligned with the BI-RADS concept. (E-)BI-RADS categories 4 and 5 were considered an indication for biopsy. Histopathologic evaluation or imaging follow-up served as the reference standard. RESULTS: The cohort comprised 344 breast lesions in 337 patients, including 224 (65.1%) malignant and 120 (34.9%) benign lesions. B-mode BI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 98.6% (221/224) and a specificity of 34.2% (41/120). E-BI-RADS demonstrated malignancy rates of 0.0% in E-BI-RADS 2 (0/71); 5.3% in E-BI-RADS 3 (1/19); 85.2% in E-BI-RADS 4 (155/182); and 94.4% in E-BI-RADS 5 (68/70). E-BI-RADS achieved a sensitivity of 99.6% (223/224) and a specificity of 74.2% (89/120). The single false-negative case was a 31 mm B-cell lymphoma, classified as E-BI-RADS 3, with a shear-wave velocity of 4.4 m/s and an E/B ratio of 0.9. Decision-curve analysis demonstrates that E-BI-RADS achieves higher net benefit than SWE-based and B-mode BI-RADS strategies. DISCUSSION: E-BI-RADS provides the first standardized, BI-RADS-like classification system for breast elastography and enables safe biopsy de-escalation with excellent sensitivity and improved specificity compared with existing approaches.

articles.title: Handling Consults with Poise: A Practical Guide to Phone and In-Person Consults for Radiology Trainees.
Portal Vein Recanalization in Children with Extrahepatic Portal Vein Obstruction: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To synthesize the technical success, safety, durability, and clinical efficacy of percutaneous portal vein recanalization in children with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction without underlying liver disease. MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science were searched from inception to May 2026 for pediatric patients with non-cirrhotic extrahepatic portal vein obstruction who underwent percutaneous portal vein recanalization. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals and prediction intervals. RESULTS: Five retrospective single-center cohorts (73 children; variceal bleeding, hypersplenism, or both) were included. Pooled denominators were 67 for technical success, 54 for safety and mortality (Pimpalwar contributed to technical success only), and 16 for post-recanalization durability. Technical success was 55.0% (95% confidence interval 41.0-68.0; prediction interval 28.6-79.4). Procedure-related and all-cause mortality were both 0% (0/54); procedure-related hemorrhage 7% (95% confidence interval 2-23); and portal-biliary fistula 3% (95% confidence interval 0-27). Among the 16 children with successful recanalization and imaging follow-up, assisted portal vein patency was 87% (95% confidence interval 61-97); 50.8% required at least one endovascular re-intervention during surveillance, without surgical conversion; freedom from recurrent variceal or gastrointestinal bleeding among those with variceal bleeding as indication was 100% (prediction interval 73.8-100). CONCLUSION: In children with chronic native-vessel extrahepatic portal vein obstruction, percutaneous portal vein recanalization may be feasible. No procedure-related mortality was observed, bleeding events were infrequent, and no recurrent variceal bleeding occurred after successful recanalization in patients for whom this outcome was reported. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, meta-analysis of case series and retrospective cohort studies. TRIAL / PROTOCOL REGISTRATION: Prospectively registered with the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO): CRD420261395918.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence methods for HER2 status assessment: a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an important predictive and prognostic biomarker that guides targeted therapy, particularly in breast and gastric cancers. Conventional HER2 assessment using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is limited by inter-observer variability, heterogeneous expression, and diagnostic complexity. This systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to evaluate Artificial Intelligence-based HER2 assessment. Fifty-one studies were included in the qualitative synthesis and 14 in the diagnostic meta-analysis. Bibliometric analysis, methodological taxonomy, comparative evaluation, and pooled diagnostic performance were assessed, with study quality evaluated using QUADAS-2. AI methodologies have rapidly evolved from conventional machine learning and radiomics to deep learning, Vision Transformers, explainable AI, and multimodal frameworks, with histopathology and Magnetic Resonance Imaging. being the most frequently used modalities. Research activity increased markedly between 2023 and 2025. Pooled sensitivity was 87.8%, specificity was 83.5%, and Summary Receiver Operating Characteristic Area Under the Curve (SROC AUC) was 0.852 (95% CI: 0.801-0.881), indicating promising overall diagnostic performance. Deeks' funnel plot asymmetry test showed no significant evidence of publication bias (p = 0.14). However, heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates. Heterogeneous datasets, limited external validation, and inconsistent evaluation methods remain important barriers to clinical implementation. Future research should emphasize multicenter prospective validation, explainable and multimodal AI, foundation models, federated learning, and evaluation in underexplored malignancies, including gallbladder cancer.

articles.title: CT-based machine learning and multimodal prediction in acute pancreatitis: a narrative review.
articles.abstract: Acute pancreatitis (AP) has a highly variable clinical course. This narrative review focuses on computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep learning and clinical-imaging models for severity and adverse-outcome prediction, with clinical-only models as context. A targeted PubMed search checked on 16 October 2026, with a publication cutoff of 14 October 2026, retrieved 80 unique records; ten CT-informed exemplars and eight clinical-context studies were selected for detailed comparison. This is a representative, non-exhaustive synthesis. For severe AP (SAP) prediction, reported same-center internal or temporal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) ranged from 0.852 to 0.894, and reported external-test AUCs from 0.887 to 0.916; one validation cohort of unconfirmed independence had an AUC of 0.920. These descriptive ranges do not establish model superiority or characterize all retrieved studies. CT protocols and input timing, endpoint definitions, sampling and validation designs varied. Predominantly retrospective evidence, uncertain prediction landmarks, incomplete calibration and threshold reporting, and limited prospective impact assessment constrain translation. Feature explanations describe model associations rather than causal intervention targets. Imaging artificial intelligence (AI) remains an adjunct to clinical assessment; independent validation, calibration, decision-curve appraisal and prospective workflow/outcome evaluation are needed before clinical-pathway integration.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and safety reporting after image-guided and non-image-guided subtalar joint injections: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Subtalar joint (STJ) injections are used for chronic hindfoot pain but evidence comparing guidance methods remains limited. METHODS: This systematic review followed PRISMA 2020. PubMed, Embase (via Ovid), Scopus and Web of Science were searched from inception to December 2025, and the searches were re-run in a broadened form in July 2026. Eligible studies included comparative studies, single-arm cohort or case-series studies with 10 or more procedures and technical/cadaveric accuracy studies reporting subtalar-specific outcomes. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. Heterogeneity and scarce direct comparison precluded meta-analysis. RESULTS: Seventeen studies were eligible: 12 reported clinical data and five reported cadaveric technical accuracy data only (one clinical study also contributed a cadaveric control arm). Denominators are reported in their own units and are not combined: the clinical studies contributed 129 patients (six studies), 100 injected joints (four studies) and 779 injections (two studies). Ultrasound, fluoroscopy and landmark-guided injection were each reported in five studies. No study of CT or SPECT-CT guidance provided a subtalar-specific outcome. Needle placement accuracy ranged from 68 to 100%, but difference in design, populations and confirmation methods prevented comparison between modalities. CONCLUSION: STJ injections are associated with clinical improvement but evidence is predominantly observational and heterogeneous. Differences in reporting technical accuracy, injectate, clinical response and adverse events prevent comparison of guidance methods. No modality's superiority is established. Prospective comparative studies using standardised outcomes and consistent safety reporting are needed.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence in Orthopedic Image Analysis: A Systematic Review and Unified Taxonomy of Bone Age Assessment and Fracture Detection.
articles.abstract: Bone age assessment (BAA) and fracture detection are essential tasks in orthopedic radiography, since they aid diagnosis and clinical decision-making in trauma treatment. Recent technologies in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly deep learning (DL), have enhanced the ability to analyze radiological images with greater accuracy and consistency. However, current studies are incomplete, with inconsistent evaluation methodologies, limited external validation, and insufficient interpretability, limiting clinical implementation. This study provides a systematic PRISMA-based review of 116 studies (2017-2025) that analyze imaging modalities, datasets, model architectures, evaluation techniques, and clinical relevance. A uniform taxonomy is introduced to define techniques based on task, modality, and learning paradigm, along with a comparative methodology to address inconsistencies across studies. The findings indicate that CNN and transformer-based models achieve MAE as low as 0.4-0.7 years and accuracy exceeding 95% in controlled datasets but are limited by dataset bias, poor generalization, and a lack of standardized benchmarks. Although explainable AI (XAI) approaches increase interpretability, their clinical reliability is still limited. This review synthesizes current methodologies, identifies key problems, and proposes future directions for AI systems that are robust, interpretable, and clinically deployable, while unifying BAA and fracture detection under a single taxonomy that integrates modality, task, and learning paradigm.

articles.title: CT-based Epicardial Adipose Tissue Change as a Promising Biomarker of Obstructive Coronary Artery Disease Progression: A Longitudinal Observational Study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the association between CT-based longitudinal changes in epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) volume and obstructive coronary artery disease (CAD) progression. METHODS: We included 583 suspected CAD patients (median age, 60 years; 348 men) who underwent coronary CT angiography (CCTA) between June 2010 and June 2017, and received follow-up CCTA at an interval of ≥ 2 years (median interval, 3.33 years; IQR, 2.67 to 4.33 years). 107 patients progressed to obstructive CAD. EAT volume and coronary artery calcium score (CACS) were measured on non-contrast CCTA. Annualised EAT volume change was calculated as the difference between follow-up and baseline scans divided by the follow-up duration. Obstructive CAD progression was defined as new-onset ≥50% stenosis in initially non-obstructive patients. The association of EAT with obstructive CAD progression was evaluated by univariate and multivariate logistic regression. RESULTS: Annualised EAT volume change was 3.47 cm³ in the obstructive progression group and 2.07 cm³ in the no obstructive progression group (P = 0.006). In univariate analysis, only age, CACS, baseline largest luminal diameter stenosis and annualised EAT volume change were significantly associated with obstructive CAD progression. Annualised EAT volume change remained independently associated with obstructive CAD progression (adjusted OR = 1.06, P = 0.007) after adjustment for variables significant in univariate analysis. CONCLUSIONS: Annualised EAT volume change was independently associated with obstructive CAD progression. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Annualised EAT volume change may represent a CT-based imaging marker of obstructive CAD progression.

articles.title: Beyond the Screening Paradigm: Why NHS Symptomatic Breast Services Require Bespoke AI Monitoring Parameters.
Machine learning-based experimental access to photon-by-photon arrival times in scintillation detectors.
articles.abstract: Objective. Scintillation detectors with excellent timing resolution enable more precise localization of radiation sources in positron emission tomography, leading to substantial improvements in diagnostic capability for diseases such as cancer and dementia. At the timing precision required for such applications at the picosecond scale, detector performance is governed by the dynamics of scintillation photons generated within the detector and their subsequent detection processes. However, detector signals have conventionally been treated only as collective responses of many photons due to structural constraints inherent to photodetectors. In this study, we overcome this fundamental limitation using deep learning framework.Approach. The proposed method estimates photon-by-photon arrival times directly from detector waveforms without requiring any modification to the detector structure; the method operates on an event-by-event basis without ground-truth labels by integrating an unsupervised learning framework with a physically informed detector-response model.Main results. Through comprehensive validation combining Monte Carlo simulation and experimental measurements across various detector configurations, we experimentally demonstrate improved timing resolution, visualized depth-of-interaction-dependent photon transport, and classified Cherenkov and scintillation photons based on the estimated photon-level timing information using a unified deep learning-based framework.Significance. These results provide experimental access to photon dynamics, bridging the gap between theoretical modeling and experimental observation, and they open a new data-driven pathway for discovery in detector physics and optimization.

articles.title: Incidental Findings in Asymptomatic Healthy Individuals Screened with Total-Body Ultra-Low-Dose 18F-FDG-PET/Low-Dose CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the prevalence and clinical significance of incidental findings (IF) detected by Total-body 18F-Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography (FDG-PET/CT) in a genuinely asymptomatic cohort of blood donors. METHODS: 117 healthy, asymptomatic blood donors underwent ultra-low-dose FDG-PET/low-dose CT. The primary objective was to create an atlas of glucose metabolism in healthy individuals. A secondary objective was to assess the frequency and nature of IF, informing future considerations of the clinical value of potential screening programs. Here we report on IF. RESULTS: IF were detected in 64 participants (55%), with 51 (44%) presenting clinically insignificant IF and 13 (11%) clinically significant IF. Common insignificant IF included benign or inflammatory metabolic activity in the esophagus or lung parenchyma (n = 19), metabolically active reactive lymph nodes (n = 14), and degenerative skeletal changes (n = 13). Clinically significant IF comprised pathologically metabolically active cysts and polyps (n = 8), significantly enlarged vessels (n = 1), suspected malignant tumors (n = 1), large lipomas (n = 1), sarcoidosis (n = 1), and liver steatosis (n = 1). CONCLUSIONS: This is the first study to systematically investigate incidental findings in an asymptomatic cohort using ultra-low-dose total-body FDG-PET/CT. Even in this highly selected population, numerous IFs were revealed, underscoring the need for risk-stratified, data-driven screening strategies integrating genetic biomarkers identifying individuals who will truly benefit. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: This first study of ultra-low-dose total-body FDG-PET/CT in asymptomatic donors found frequent incidental findings (55%, 11% clinically significant), establishing lower-bound estimates and supporting risk-stratified screening approaches.

articles.title: Feature-Level Fourier Amplitude Modulation to Reduce Domain-Specific Spectral Bias for Cross-Domain Polyp Segmentation.
articles.abstract: Accurate polyp segmentation is critical for early colorectal cancer detection, yet models trained on one endoscopic dataset often degrade during cross-domain evaluation. One major source of this gap is acquisition-induced appearance variation, where imaging settings and post-processing pipelines introduce color shifts that encourage models to rely on domain-specific cues. Existing image-level Fourier amplitude approaches reduce global appearance discrepancy but align the entire image spectrum before feature extraction, which risks coupling mucosal background statistics with polyp-relevant signals. We instead modulate the Fourier amplitude of encoder features. Specifically, we decompose the feature amplitude into low- and high-frequency bands and recalibrate their second-order amplitude statistics in a projected space, while preserving the original phase. Since spectral modulation can attenuate fine boundary-related high-frequency responses, we complement it with directional edge refinement guided by an auxiliary luminance signal. Extensive experiments across five polyp segmentation benchmarks under cross-domain protocols show consistent improvements over strong baselines. Quantitatively, the proposed method attains the highest Dice on all five benchmarks (0.930 on Kvasir-SEG and 0.938 on CVC-ClinicDB in-domain; 0.891, 0.805, and 0.830 on the unseen CVC-300, CVC-ColonDB, and ETIS datasets).

articles.title: Benchmark Accuracy Does Not Transfer: Domain Adaptive Deep Learning for Diabetic Retinopathy Detection in a Bangladeshi Clinical Setting.
articles.abstract: Deep learning could make diabetic retinopathy (DR) screening more accessible where ophthalmologists are scarce, but high benchmark accuracy does not guarantee reliable clinical performance. We investigate this gap using 3662 images from APTOS 2019 for source training and a balanced evaluation corpus of 500 fundus images (250 DR, 250 No-DR) from a Bangladeshi clinic, graded by a single experienced ophthalmologist. Source-trained models achieved 94.26-96.80% accuracy under tenfold cross-validation on APTOS, yet achieved only 49.4-50.6% (mean 50.0%) when applied directly to the clinical images. The resulting 44.46-46.85 percentage-point losses across all six architectures provide consistent quantitative evidence of severe domain shift. A full-cohort feature comparison yielded a classical-feature Fréchet distance of 133.49 and an MMD   2  of 0.3967 (permutation p = 0.0005  ). To recover target-domain performance, we evaluate an adaptation pipeline that integrates retinal-specific preprocessing, progressive fine-tuning with discriminative learning rates, soft-voting inference, and test-time augmentation. Aggregated out-of-fold evaluation produced 81.0% accuracy (95% Wilson CI 77.3-84.2%), 70.0% sensitivity, 92.0% specificity, 89.7% precision, and a 78.7% F1 score. Fine-tuning increased mean individual-model accuracy by 27.1 percentage points, whereas preprocessing contributed a descriptive 2.0-point increase. These findings quantify a substantial benchmark-to-clinic gap and show that target-domain adaptation can improve performance, while the remaining false-negative rate and single-clinic design preclude claims of clinical readiness.

articles.title: ConvFormer3D: A Hybrid 3D-CNN-Transformer Front-End for Cine cMRI View Classification Pipelines.
articles.abstract: It is vital to reliably identify the views of standard cine cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (cine cMRI), since each determines which cardiac anatomy will be observed and undergo quantitative analysis. If the view is incorrectly identified, whether by a human observer or by an automated system, errors can propagate into subsequent analyses that give rise to the volumetric assessment, strain analysis, evaluation of the valves, and thus diagnostics. Accurate classification remains a challenge due to clinical variation between scanner manufacturers, differences in acquisition protocols, and motion artifacts. This study presents ConvFormer3D, a hybrid spatiotemporal architecture that includes a Kinetics-400-pretrained 3D residual encoder (R3D-18), modified to handle single-channel cine input, combined with a lightweight temporal transformer and attention-based token pooling. The convolutional stages supply local anatomical and motion priors, while the temporal transformer captures time dependencies throughout the cardiac cycle at full temporal resolution. The network is trained using deep auxiliary supervision, label smoothing, an exponential moving average of the parameters, and mixed-precision optimization. The model's predicted probabilities are then calibrated by temperature scaling. To prevent data leakage, the different partitions are created at the level of the individual patient, and all reported metrics are recorded at patient-clustered bootstraps at the 95% confidence interval, together with formal paired significance testing between the various models. On a separate patient-level test partition, ConvFormer3D achieved an accuracy of 0.983 and an expected calibration error of 0.003 after temperature scaling.

articles.title: SPBA-Net: A Comparative Feature Enhancement Network for Midbrain Segmentation in Transcranial Sonography.
articles.abstract: Segmentation of the midbrain during transcranial sonography is an essential step in the ultrasound evaluation of Parkinson's disease. However, this method is limited by issues such as low imaging resolution, unclear anatomical boundaries, and poor contrast between tissues. We propose a comparative feature enhancement network called SPBA-Net, which mitigates these shortcomings. The framework first employs a learnable butterfly-shaped prior guidance module (LSPG) to ensure anatomical consistency and embeds a gated boundary enhancement unit (BEA) in the decoder to reduce edge blurring. Furthermore, we introduce a sparse non-local attention mechanism (SNLA) and an adaptive multiscale fusion module (ASFM) to efficiently capture long-range feature dependencies. Finally, we design a dynamically gated reverse attention compensation module (DGRC) to address the foreground-background imbalance and integrate a composite multiscale loss function. In the midbrain segmentation task, SPBA-Net outperformed mainstream baseline models on all evaluation metrics, achieving a DSC of 0.9556 while maintaining reasonable computational overhead. In addition, this model is also applicable to segmentation tasks involving other objects and other modalities. This indicates that the proposed SPBA-Net not only facilitates automated quantitative analysis of the midbrain in the future but can also be transferred to other segmentation tasks.

articles.title: Learnable Pixel-Level Reward Modeling and Pixel-Wise Probability Mixing for Semi-supervised Medical Image Segmentation.
articles.abstract: In semi-supervised medical image segmentation, pseudo-labeling and data mixing are widely adopted to leverage unlabeled images, yet conventional methods suffer from coarse-grained operations. Specifically, global filtering strategies typically rely on heuristic confidence scores that may not accurately reflect local pseudo-label reliability and apply spatially uniform loss weights to all pixels within retained samples, failing to reliably evaluate and accommodate spatial quality variations within pseudo-labels. Meanwhile, coarse-grained region-level mixing violently disrupts the inherent continuity of anatomical structures, frequently introducing severe semantic mismatches and misleading boundary targets during training. To address these limitations, we propose a semi-supervised segmentation framework based on learnable pixel-level reward modeling and pixel-wise probability mixing. A data-driven pixel-level reward map is constructed to provide learnable pixel-level reliability estimation instead of relying solely on heuristic confidence scores. These continuous reward scores are directly converted into fine-grained pixel-wise loss weights, dynamically regulating each pixel's optimization contribution rather than relying on hard confidence-based sample filtering; an empty-foreground safeguard only suppresses degenerate unlabeled samples with negligible predicted foreground. Furthermore, local pseudo-label distributions are adaptively refined via pixel-wise probability mixing within the continuous class probability space. This mechanism softly fuses the probability distributions of low-reward pixels with those of semantically consistent high-reward donor pixels, successfully bypassing the structural constraints of region-level mixing. Extensive experiments on the ACDC, BUSI, and Synapse datasets demonstrate consistent improvements over competitive semi-supervised baselines under limited labeled-data settings.

articles.title: Selective Retrieval Routing for Finding-Oriented Chest Radiograph Text Generation: A Locked Policy Evaluation.
articles.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation is increasingly used in medical text systems, but its value may depend on when it is activated. We evaluated retrieval as a case-level routing decision for finding-oriented chest radiograph text generation. Five policies were compared using a frozen visual generator, the official PadChest-GR split (3185 training, 455 validation, and 915 test studies), and a locked evaluation pipeline. The primary outcome was six-label clinical F1. Retrieval burden was quantified as the mean number of retrieved neighbors per study, and the Lexical Overlap Index measured surface overlap. Sensitivity analyses included 1000 matched random gates and an exploratory blinded review of 100 cases by three reviewers. Six-label clinical F1 was 0.3488 with No Retrieval and 0.2670 with Always Retrieval. Risk-only top 60% achieved the highest observed value among the evaluated policies (0.3703), with a paired-bootstrap difference of + 0.02157 (95% CI, 0.01707 to 0.02654) versus No Retrieval. Matched random routing achieved 0.3020 ± 0.0053, and no seed reached the Risk-only result. In blinded review, Always Retrieval produced fewer reviewer-assessed acceptable outputs and more unsupported findings than No Retrieval. Risk-only routing did not show a clear acceptability advantage over No Retrieval and had a directionally higher unsupported-finding proportion. These findings indicate that automatic metric gains should be interpreted separately from demonstrated clinical quality.

articles.title: Guardrail-Based Radiology Protocolling with Large Language Models: Balancing Automation and Oversight.
articles.abstract: Safe clinical deployment of large language models (LLMs) for radiology protocolling requires knowing when not to automate. We evaluated a "guardrail-first" workflow that defers incomplete or safety-critical CT and MRI requests to radiologists before assignment. In this single-center retrospective study, 537 body imaging requests were temporally split into prompt development (n = 109) and validation (n = 428) cohorts. An expert radiologist classified requests as protocol-eligible or requiring review. Six LLM pipelines (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.2 high, DeepSeek V3.2, and DeepSeek V3.2 reasoner) were evaluated in two stages (review triage, protocol assignment) against human protocolers. Primary outcome was clinically appropriate assignment (exact/equivalent protocol or correct review escalation), with bootstrapped 95% CIs. The expert reference standard classified 57/428 requests (13.3%) as requiring review (15 safety-critical, 23 major missing information, 19 minor clarification). For the 38 requests with safety-critical issues or major missing information, Gemini 3.1 Pro achieved 100% sensitivity (38/38; 95% CI, 90.7-100), versus 94.7%-97.4% for other pipelines. Among 371 protocol-eligible requests, unnecessary escalation ranged from 1.3% (5/371) to 34.0% (126/371), remaining lowest for reasoning-enabled models. The human benchmark achieved 83.6% (95% CI, 79.8-87.3) exact/equivalent assignment, exceeded by Gemini 3.1 Pro (+12.7 percentage points; 95% CI, 8.6-16.7), Claude Sonnet 4.6 (+12.4; 8.4-16.4), GPT-5.2 high (+11.6; 7.3-15.9), and DeepSeek V3.2 reasoner (+8.6; 4.3-12.9). End-to-end clinically appropriate assignment ranged from 65.0% (60.5-69.4) for GPT-5.2 to 96.3% (94.4-97.9) for Gemini 3.1 Pro; the three highest-performing pipelines did not differ significantly. A guardrail-first LLM protocolling workflow combined high-performance automation with reliable identification of requests requiring radiologist review, supporting further prospective evaluation.

articles.title: Assessment of Vestibular Schwannoma Growth After Radiosurgery: Variability in Clinical Decision Thresholds and the Role of Artificial Intelligence.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To quantify expert interobserver variability in longitudinal vestibular schwannoma growth assessment after radiosurgery and evaluate AI segmentation performance relative to human variability. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Retrospective review of patients with sporadic unilateral VS treated with stereotactic radiosurgery (2001-2023). Manual and AI segmentations were compared across the cohort. A growth-enriched subset of 24 tumors underwent additional expert assessment. Agreement was evaluated using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC), Fleiss and Cohen κ, Bland-Altman analysis, and Dice similarity coefficients. RESULTS: The cohort included 170 MRI examinations from 85 patients (45.9% female; median age, 66 years; median follow-up, 53 months). Human interobserver agreement was excellent for baseline volume (ICC, 0.95), follow-up volume (ICC, 0.98), and percent volume change (ICC, 0.89), but decreased for ≥ 20% growth classification (Fleiss κ, 0.52). Eleven of 24 tumors met the strict-majority growth definition. AI-expert agreement was excellent for baseline and follow-up volumes (ICC, 0.99 and 0.97), but lower for percent change (ICC, 0.83). AI achieved 83.5% binary agreement (Cohen κ, 0.47) and median Dice coefficient of 0.85 (IQR, 0.77-0.90). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean bias of + 6.64 percentage points (95% limits of agreement, - 53.33 to 66.60). CONCLUSIONS: AI-human agreement for absolute tumor volumes was comparable to human interobserver agreement. However, longitudinal growth assessment and binary classification demonstrated greater variability, emphasizing the importance of benchmarking AI performance against human variability when applying clinically relevant growth thresholds.

articles.title: Conformalized Semi-Supervised Learning for Medical Imaging.
articles.abstract: To investigate whether conformal prediction (CP)-based uncertainty quantification (UQ) can improve semi-supervised learning (SSL) frameworks. Five machine learning (ML) frameworks were developed and evaluated: supervised learning (SL), standard SSL, iterative SSL, conformalized SSL (CSSL), and iterative CSSL. Logistic regression (LR) models were trained using radiomics features extracted from MRI and CT datasets across three classification tasks: isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation prediction in gliomas, O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase (MGMT) promoter methylation prediction in gliomas, and histopathological classification in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Model performance was evaluated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) and the area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) with 95% confidence intervals, and statistical comparisons were performed using DeLong's test. Across all three tasks, uncertainty-aware SSL frameworks outperformed conventional SL and standard SSL approaches. For IDH prediction, CSSL and iterative CSSL demonstrated statistically significant improvements compared with SL and SSL (p < 0.05). For MGMT prediction, iterative SSL, CSSL, and iterative CSSL significantly outperformed SL (p < 0.05). Similarly, in NSCLC histology classification, iterative SSL and CSSL-based methods significantly improved performance compared with SL (p < 0.05).
