Integrating CP into SSL frameworks improves pseudo-label reliability by filtering uncertain predictions and reducing error propagation during self-training. The proposed uncertainty-aware SSL approaches demonstrated improved performance across multiple radiomics-based classification tasks, highlighting their potential utility in medical imaging applications where labeled data are limited but unlabeled data are abundant.

articles.title: Five-year Survival after Conventional Transarterial Chemoembolization for Hepatocellular Carcinoma: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Observational Cohorts.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To systematically review and meta-analyze reported five-year survival after superselective conventional transarterial chemoembolization for hepatocellular carcinoma and characterize the clinical and procedural factors limiting its interpretation. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This registered systematic review and meta-analysis searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and Ichushi-Web through March 7, 2026. Core eligibility required iodized-oil-based treatment at a subsegmental or more distal tumor-feeder level; three previously defined procedural or cohort extensions were retained. Two reviewers independently evaluated the reports. Reported 60-month survival was pooled using random-effects logit models with Hartung-Knapp confidence intervals. Treatment periods, drugs, embolic materials, and available liver-function and tumor-stage strata were examined. RESULTS: Twenty-eight reports were included; six overlap-adjudicated cohorts comprising 790 patients contributed to the synthesis. Pooled five-year survival was 55.6% (Hartung-Knapp 95% confidence interval, 41.6-68.8%; prediction interval, 28.7-79.6%). Child-Pugh A-only cohorts (198 patients), A/B cohorts without reported C (393 patients), and the A/B/C cohort (199 patients) reported survival of 52.0%-74.5%, 49.0%-64.8%, and 38.8%, respectively. Five-year survival among 32 Child-Pugh C patients was 27.1%. Exploratory treatment-period pooling yielded 47.1% (95% confidence interval, 28.0-67.1%) before 2010 and 63.2% (30.1-87.2%) from 2010 onward; these descriptive subgroup estimates do not establish an adjusted era effect. Tumor profiles differed, and later cohorts used cone-beam CT, guidance software, or angiography-CT. CONCLUSION: Pooled five-year survival was numerically higher in later cohorts, emphasizing the need for comparable Child-Pugh class, tumor burden, and clearly characterized procedures when comparing contemporary treatments. Level of Evidence Level 4, systematic review and meta-analysis of retrospective observational cohorts.

articles.title: High-Frequency Ultrasound Combined with Percutaneous Lymphatic Contrast-Enhanced Ultrasound for Preoperative Localization of Lymphaticovenous Anastomosis in Perineal Lymphedema.
articles.abstract: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES: Lymphaticovenous anastomosis (LVA) is an effective surgical procedure for perineal lymphedema by reconstructing lymphatic pathways. The success of LVA highly depends on accurate preoperative identification and localization of functional lymphatic vessels and corresponding superficial venules. This study aimed to assess the feasibility of high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) combined with percutaneous lymphatic contrast-enhanced ultrasound (PL-CEUS) for identifying the optimal anastomotic site for LVA surgery in patients with perineal lymphedema. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included 54 patients with perineal lymphedema who underwent LVA. Preoperatively, functional lymphatic vessels were identified and localized via intradermal injection of a contrast agent combined with HFUS. The accuracy of ultrasound localization was calculated based on intraoperative exploration as the gold standard. The diameter and depth of functional lymphatic vessels and matched superficial small veins were measured and analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 196 functional lymphatic vessels were successfully identified and localized in 54 patients using HFUS combined with PL-CEUS. The mean internal diameter and depth of the lymphatic vessels were 0.37±0.17 mm and 8.44±3.07 mm, respectively. The mean internal diameter and mean depth of the matched superficial small veins were 0.61±0.25 mm and 5.99±3.27 mm, respectively. Surgical exploration confirmed that the localization accuracy of lymphatic vessels using the combined ultrasound technique was 95.45%. CONCLUSION: HFUS combined with PL-CEUS enabled precise preoperative planning of the optimal anastomotic site for LVA in patients with perineal lymphedema.

articles.title: Truncal Marginal Veins in CLOVES and PIK3CA-Related Overgrowth Spectrum: Anatomic Patterns and Potential Clinical Insights for Diagnosis and Endovascular Treatments.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To describe the anatomy, clinical features, and endovascular treatment outcomes of truncal marginal veins (TMVs) involving the chest or abdominal wall in patients with Congenital Lipomatous Overgrowth, Vascular Malformations, Epidermal nevi, and Skeletal abnormalities (CLOVES) and PIK3CA-related overgrowth spectrum (PROS). MATERIALS AND METHODS: The Vascular Anomalies Center database was retrospectively reviewed from 2008 to January 2026 to identify patients with TMVs. Imaging was reviewed for TMV diameter, origin, and insertion. Patient demographics, endovascular treatments, and follow-up data were analyzed. RESULTS: Thirty-two patients (53% male; median age 4.2 years; CLOVES [n=26], PROS [n=6]) with 44 TMVs were included. TMVs were unilateral in 20 patients and bilateral in 12. The median TMV diameter was 9.0 mm. TMVs most commonly originated from the abdominal wall (n=21), followed by the chest wall (n=9), saphenofemoral junction (n=9), and lateral marginal vein (n=5). The most common insertion site was axillary vein (n=39) followed by the abdominal wall (n=5). Thirty embolization procedures were performed in 25 patients; a single embolic agent was used in 20 procedures and multiple agents in 10. The most commonly used agents were coils (n=26) and n-butyl cyanoacrylate glue (n=9). No treatment-related adverse events occurred. Among 26 treated TMVs with imaging follow-up (median 23 months), partial recanalization occurred in two TMVs (8%), whereas 24 (92%) remained completely occluded. CONCLUSION: In this predominantly CLOVES cohort, TMVs most often arise from the abdominal wall and drain into the axillary vein, and endovascular treatment of TMVs appears safe, effective, and durable on imaging follow-up.

articles.title: OCCLUDE: Final Results from the Prospective Multicenter Real-World Study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of Obsidio Conformable Embolic for vascular embolization. MATERIALS AND METHODS: OCCLUDE is a multicenter, prospective, single-arm, real-world clinical registry. Patients (n=125) from 19 centers underwent embolization with Obsidio and were followed for 1 month. The primary effectiveness endpoint was technical success, defined as occlusion of target vessel(s), confirmed by angiography or visualization of an Obsidio cast on fluoroscopy/imaging immediately post-embolization. Clinical success, a secondary endpoint, was defined as absence of target vessel bleeding within 30 days. The primary safety endpoint was freedom from major adverse events (MAEs), defined as non-target embolization meeting serious adverse event criteria, unintended target organ/soft tissue infarction, vessel perforation/injury, or catheter entrapment through 30 days. RESULTS: Indications included bleeding/hemorrhage (n=98; 78.4%), hypervascular tumor (HVT; n=19; 15.2%), and other (n=8; 6.4%). Median age was 63.0 years; 88.8% (n=111) had a single target embolized. Target arteries were renal (25.5%), non-gastrointestinal (GI) visceral (17.4%), upper GI (9.3%), extremity (3.7%), lower GI (2.5%), and other (41.6%). Among 161 embolized vessels, 38 (23.6%) received another embolic with Obsidio, with 84.2% used before Obsidio. Technical success was 100%. Clinical success was assessed in hemorrhage (n=98) and bleeding HVT (n=7) cases (n=105 total). Clinical success was 100% among 97/105 evaluable patients (0% rebleeding); 8 lacked 30-day follow-up. Freedom from MAEs was 97.4% (113/116), and no catheter entrapment occurred. CONCLUSIONS: OCCLUDE demonstrated real-world safety and effectiveness of Obsidio, achieving 100% technical and clinical success, with a low MAE rate across diverse target vessels.

articles.title: Particle therapy for T3N0M0 non-small cell lung cancer: a Japanese nationwide prospective registry study.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Particle therapy offers dosimetric advantages over conventional photon therapy, potentially minimizing toxicities for larger tumors. This study evaluated the clinical outcomes and safety of particle therapy for cT3N0M0 non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) using a Japanese nationwide prospective registry. METHODS: This multicenter prospective observational registry study included patients with cT3N0M0 NSCLC who were treated with proton beam therapy or carbon-ion radiotherapy between May 2016 and June 2021. Overall survival (OS), progression-free survival (PFS), cumulative incidence of local failure (LF), and adverse events were evaluated. Prognostic factors were compared using the Cox proportional hazards model and the cumulative incidence curves were compared using the Fine-Gray model. RESULTS: A total of 96 patients were evaluated. With a median follow-up of 53 months, the 3-year OS, PFS, and LF rates were 48.1 %, 33.0 %, and 19.2 %, respectively. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were observed in 5 patients (5.2 %), with no Grade 5 events reported. In multivariate analysis, concomitant interstitial lung disease and low vital capacity were identified as significant prognostic factors for both OS and PFS. No statistically significant associations with OS or PFS were detected for tumor size > 5 cm, treatment modality, or chemotherapy. CONCLUSION: Particle therapy showed encouraging survival outcomes and a low reported incidence of severe toxicity in patients with cT3N0M0 NSCLC, potentially offering a definitive treatment option for those who are medically inoperable or decline surgery.

articles.title: Impact of lung cancer screening on the workload of radiology professionals.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Lung cancer screening (LCS) with low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) significantly reduces mortality among high-risk individuals, yet implementation remains limited at national and European levels. The Strengthening the Screening of Lung Cancer (SOLACE) Project aims to facilitate the implementation of equitable LCS. While considering the overall impact of LCS, we identified a lack of systematic evaluation on the impact on the workload of radiology professionals, including radiologists and radiographers. This multicentric, European-wide study prospectively examines the effects of LCS on radiology healthcare workers. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A survey-based cross-sectional study was conducted among European radiology professionals engaged in LCS to evaluate their experiences across seven domains: impacts on workload, workflow specifics, reporting practices, artificial intelligence (AI) use, participation in training programmes, potential professional development, and overall support for LCS. RESULTS: We evaluated 56 responses (mean age 46 ± 10.8 years; 27 men) from 14 countries. About half of respondents (53.6%; n = 30) reported increased working hours, but only 21.6% (n = 11) felt overworked due to LCS. No significant factors were directly associated with feeling overworked. Most respondents (86.7%; n = 39) perceived increased expertise in assessing LCS LDCTs throughout screening, and 91.1% (n = 51) expressed support for the implementation of LCS. CONCLUSION: Although LCS increased workload for many radiology professionals, few reported feeling overworked. Despite the added demands, there may be added benefits for radiology professionals. Taken together, these findings emphasise the importance of continuously evaluating and monitoring how LCS affects the workload of radiology healthcare professionals. KEY POINTS: Question As wider implementation of lung cancer screening occurs in Europe, it is critical to consider its impact on radiology professionals' workload and associated workforce demands. Findings Although lung cancer screening increased workload for many radiology professionals, few felt overworked, and the majority perceived increased diagnostic confidence and support for screening implementation. CRITICAL RELEVANCE STATEMENT: Lung cancer screening via LDCT plays a critical role in detecting cancer earlier and improving survival. With growing support for the broader implementation of LCS, it is essential to consider its potential impact on the workload of radiology professionals.

articles.title: Should I pursue a PhD in radiology? Opportunities, pitfalls, and practical strategies.
articles.abstract: Undertaking a PhD in radiology represents a pivotal career choice: one that can open pathways to international mobility, interdisciplinary collaboration, and scientific discovery. This opinion piece examines the opportunities and challenges of pursuing doctoral training in radiology and provides guidance for medical students, radiographers, residents, and practicing radiologists considering this academic path. Yet the process also entails risks: unrealistic goals, inadequate mentorship or institutional support (such as protected time for research, administrative support, and financial resources), and limited genuine motivation can hinder progress and satisfaction. In this expert opinion article, we highlight the natural synergy between clinical radiology and research skills. Beyond advancing academic credentials, a PhD cultivates competencies in statistics, leadership, and teamwork: skills that support careers across academia, healthcare, industry, and policy. We discuss different PhD formats, from monograph-based to publication-based structures, and offer practical advice on project selection, funding strategies, and supervisory relationships. We conclude with an overarching checklist with a compilation of questions to answer the question "Should I pursue a PhD in radiology?." By addressing both pragmatic and personal aspects, including mental well-being, this paper provides a balanced roadmap for (future) imaging professionals aiming to design meaningful and sustainable clinical research careers. KEY POINTS: Question Deciding whether to pursue a doctoral degree in radiology requires navigating complex trade-offs between clinical workloads, personal motivations and diverse program formats. Findings Successful doctoral training relies on aligning personal curiosity with realistic project scoping, accessible methodological support and careful supervisor selection. On the other hand, valuable alternative career paths and potential obstacles should also be considered before taking up the PhD challenge. Critical relevance statement Aligning personal goals, skills, and career planning with the institution's expectations can help (future) imaging professionals transition into sustainable research careers.

articles.title: Assessment of atrioventricular interaction and response to balloon pulmonary angioplasty in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension using cardiac MRI.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate atrioventricular interaction in patients with chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) and to determine the effects of balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) on reversible cardiac remodeling assessed by cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging. MATERIALS AND METHODS: In this prospective single-center study, 52 patients with CTEPH (mean age: 58 ± 11 years; 34 females) and 35 healthy controls underwent CMR imaging. Twenty-five patients (mean age: 60 ± 12 years; 19 females) who underwent BPA received follow-up CMR at a mean interval of 7 ± 5 months. Cardiac structure, function, myocardial deformation, and epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) were assessed based on cine images. RESULTS: Compared with controls, patients with CTEPH demonstrated predominant right-sided cardiac involvement, characterized by reduced right ventricular ejection fraction (p < 0.001), marked enlargement of right atrial (RA) and ventricular (RV) volumes, and severely impaired right heart strain (all p < 0.001). Left ventricular systolic function was relatively preserved, with mildly impaired global circumferential strain (p = 0.011) and a trend toward attenuated longitudinal strain (p = 0.055), whereas all left atrial (LA) strain components were markedly impaired (all p < 0.05), indicating altered atrioventricular interaction. Following BPA, the right heart structure, RV function and deformation, and LA conduit strain improved. EAT was comparable between groups and remained unchanged after BPA. CONCLUSION: CTEPH involves marked right heart systolic dysfunction and early biventricular diastolic abnormalities associated with impaired atrioventricular interaction. BPA could reverse cardiac remodeling by improving right heart structure, function, and partially recovering atrial deformation after pressure relief. KEY POINTS: Questions Atrioventricular interaction abnormalities and reversible cardiac remodeling in chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) after balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) remain insufficiently characterized. Findings CTEPH is associated with impaired right heart strain and altered atrioventricular interaction; BPA improves right heart structure and function and partially recovers atrial deformation. Critical relevance statement Cardiac MRI-derived myocardial deformation and atrial phasic function may reflect alterations in atrioventricular interaction in CTEPH and complement conventional metrics in assessing cardiac remodeling and recovery after BPA.

articles.title: Temporal lobe changes as a key diagnostic flag for hypochondroplasia.
articles.abstract: We report an infant referred for apnoeic episodes and a facial port-wine stain, prompting brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to assess for Sturge-Weber syndrome. MRI showed no leptomeningeal angiomatosis but revealed abnormal temporal lobe morphology with altered sulcation and bilateral hippocampal non-inversion, a pattern previously associated with fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3)-related skeletal dysplasia. This unexpected finding led to targeted genetic testing, which confirmed a de novo FGFR3 variant diagnostic of hypochondroplasia. Skeletal features were subtle in early infancy and became more obviously apparent later. This case highlights temporal lobe morphology as a diagnostic clue for FGFR3-related dysplasia on brain MRI performed for unrelated indications, potentially enabling earlier genetic diagnosis before clinical skeletal features emerge.

articles.title: Peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics for predicting early progression of hepatocellular carcinoma after microwave ablation: development and external validation of a clinical-radiomics model.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To develop and externally validate a peri-ablational contrast-enhanced CT radiomics model for predicting early hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression after microwave ablation (MWA) and to assess its incremental value over clinical predictors. METHODS: This retrospective multicenter study included 376 patients in training (n = 235), internal validation (n = 60), and external validation (n = 81) cohorts. Early progression was defined as local tumor progression or new intrahepatic HCC within 1 year after MWA. Radiomics features were extracted from 5-mm peri-ablational regions on multiphasic CT obtained 1-2 months after MWA. Six machine-learning algorithms and phase combinations were evaluated. The selected radiomics model was combined with independent clinical predictors. Discrimination, calibration, clinical utility, and model interpretability were assessed. RESULTS: The arterial-plus-portal venous phase (AP + PP) multilayer perceptron model achieved AUCs of 0.857, 0.815, and 0.903 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts, respectively, with performance comparable to the three-phase model. Log10 AFP and tumor size > 2 cm were independent clinical predictors. The combined clinical-radiomics model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.884, and 0.963, respectively. In external validation, sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy were 84.2%, 96.8%, and 93.8%, respectively. SHAP analysis identified the radiomics score as the most influential predictor. CONCLUSION: Peri-ablational AP + PP CT radiomics combined with AFP and tumor size demonstrated good discrimination for early HCC progression after MWA and may facilitate individualized risk assessment, pending further validation.

articles.title: Fat saturation on T2-weighted imaging in the assessment of renal masses and its impact on clear cell likelihood score categorization.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the impact of fat saturation on T2-weighted (T2W) imaging in the assessment of small renal masses (SRMs; cT1a ≤ 4 cm) with the clear cell likelihood score (ccLS). METHODS: This retrospective study included 147 histologically confirmed SRMs evaluated with MRI including non-fat saturated (NFS) and fat saturated (FS) T2W fast spin echo acquisitions. Two readers (R1, R2) assigned qualitative T2 signal categories (hypo-, iso-, hyperintense), with sequence-specific ccLS scores recalculated while all non-T2 ccLS components were held constant. Agreement, sequence-related reclassification, and inter-reader agreement were assessed for T2 signal intensity and ccLS scores. Cumulative link mixed models (CLMMs) were used to assess sequence-related shifts in ordinal category. Quantitative mass-to-cortex signal-intensity ratios were compared between sequences using Bland-Altman analysis. RESULTS: Qualitative agreement between sequences was 74% and 65% for R1 and R2, respectively. FS-T2W was associated with over four-fold greater cumulative odds of a higher qualitative T2 signal category than NFS-T2W (OR, 4.68; 95% CI, 2.91-7.52; p < 0.001), with upgrading in 20% (R1) and 30% (R2) of lesions versus downgrading in 5% for both readers. Qualitative inter-reader agreement was substantial (κ = 0.77 for NFS-T2W; κ = 0.73 for FS-T2W). Mass-to-cortex ratios were higher on FS-T2W (median 1.30 vs. 1.15; p < 0.001), corresponding to a mean proportional increase of 17.9% (95% CI, 12.4-23.4%). ccLS concordance remained high between NFS-T2W and FS-T2W (R1: 94% and R2: 90%; weighted κ = 0.944 and 0.918). FS-T2W was associated with greater cumulative odds of a higher ccLS category than NFS-T2W (OR, 4.27; 95% CI, 1.52-12.0; p = 0.006). Inter-reader agreement for ccLS was almost perfect (weighted κ = 0.98 for NFS-T2W; 0.95 for FS-T2W). CONCLUSION: Fat saturation introduces a systematic upward bias in qualitative T2 signal assessment of small renal masses. Although ccLS reclassification was less frequent and overall agreement remained high, this bias may alter ccLS assignment, particularly in lesions with inherently low T2 signal intensity, supporting standardized NFS-T2W acquisition when applying the ccLS.

articles.title: Receive-Only Coupled Wireless Radiofrequency Probe for Endocavity MR Imaging Using a pTx System.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: To enhance the SNR in MRI within a localized region of interest using a novel interventional wireless RF resonator probe combined with a dual-drive pTx system. METHODS: A dual-drive body birdcage coil was operated in a linearly-polarized mode to decouple a passive RF resonator probe from the transmit field while maintaining the resonator in a receive-only coupled mode. The resonator was fabricated using standard microfabrication techniques and tuned to the Larmor frequency of a 3T MRI system. The 10-g specific absorption rate (SAR) distribution was simulated to identify potential hot spots around the resonator prior to heating experiments. To evaluate the interaction between the resonator probe and the linearly-polarized transmit field, SNR and flip-angle distributions were measured in a phantom. In vivo imaging studies were subsequently performed using the resonator probe in conjunction with the linearly-polarized dual-drive birdcage coil. RESULTS: Temperature measurements demonstrated a normalized temperature increase of less than 0.10°C, corresponding to a SAR value below 1.2 W/kg. Experimental flip-angle mapping confirmed effective magnetic decoupling of the resonator probe using linearly-polarized dual-drive transmission. An SNR enhancement factor of 1.6 was achieved within the region of interest in phantom experiments. In vivo imaging demonstrated a 2.0 ± 0.2-fold SNR enhancement in the vicinity of the resonator probe. CONCLUSION: A novel interventional approach for localized SNR enhancement in MRI was demonstrated using a wireless RF resonator probe and a dual-drive pTx system. The proposed technique enables local signal enhancement while minimizing transmit-field interactions, thereby facilitating safe interventional MRI and potentially improving image quality and diagnostic performance.

articles.title: A Comprehensive Radiomics Model for Predicting Progression-Free Survival in High-Risk Neuroblastoma Based on CT Imaging.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: This study evaluates the predictive utility of clinical features, CT imaging characteristics, radiomic features, and multimodal statistical models in estimating progression-free survival (PFS) in high-risk neuroblastoma (NB) patients. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 105 pathologically confirmed high - risk NB patients per COG criteria were retrospectively selected and divided into training (80%) and test sets (20%). Statistical models were built using clinical variables, CT features, and radiomic features, with SVM algorithms employed. Five models were assessed, including radiomics, clinical + CT, clinical + radiomics, imaging + radiomics, and combined clinical + CT + radiomics models. A nomogram was constructed to predict PFS. RESULTS: Univariate analysis found NSE > 200 μg/mL, LDH >1000 U/L, and MYCN amplification as significant poor - prognosis predictors (P < 0.05). Multivariate analysis confirmed MYCN amplification (P = 0.043) and IDRFs presence (P = 0.036) as independent risk factors. A radiomics model was built from CT scans' different phases. The combined model showed the best and most stable performance with AUC values of 0.855, 0.796, 0.856 in training, validation, and test cohorts. A nomogram integrating Rad - Score and clinical parameters from Cox regression was developed, with a C - index of 0.806 (P = 0.028) via bootstrap validation. CONCLUSION: This study validates a PFS predictive model combining clinical, CT, and radiomic features, providing a robust tool for individualized prognosis in high-risk NB patients. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Radiomics demonstrates predictive utility for progression-free survival in pediatric patients with high-risk neuroblastoma.

articles.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Procedural Efficiency of ACR TI-RADS, EU-TIRADS, and K-TIRADS in ≤ 10 mm Thyroid Nodules Using Bethesda Cytology: A Cohort of 998 Nodules.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: To compare the diagnostic performance and procedural efficiency of American College of Radiology Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR TI-RADS), European Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (EU-TIRADS), and Korean Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (K-TIRADS) in ≤ 10 mm nodules using Bethesda cytology as the reference standard. METHODS: This retrospective study included 998 nodules ≤10 mm undergoing ultrasound-guided fine-needle aspiration biopsy (FNAB). Primary analyses included Bethesda II (negative) and Bethesda V-VI (positive) nodules excluding Bethesda I/III/IV, yielding 604 nodules (540 negative; 64 positive). Categories 1-3 were considered low risk and 4-5 high risk under a harmonized threshold Diagnostic performance and classification patterns were compared. RESULTS: K-TIRADS showed the numerically highest sensitivity (93.8%) and negative predictive value (NPV) (97.9%), although sensitivity did not differ significantly between systems, with lower specificity (35.4%) and accuracy (41.6%).EU-TIRADS showed intermediate performans (sensitivity 68.8%, specificity 73.7%, accuracy 73.2%). ACR TI-RADS achieved the highest specificity (83.3%) and accuracy (81.0%) with lower sensitivity (60.9%). Low-risk classification rates were 78.6% (ACR), 69.2% (EU), and 32.3% (K) of nodules; false-positive high-risk classifications among Bethesda II nodules were 16.7%, 26.3%, and 64.6%, respectively. CONCLUSION: In ≤ 10 mm nodules, the three systems demonstrated distinct diagnostic and classification profiles under a harmonized TR4-5 threshold, with different trade-offs between sensitivity and specificity. ADVANCES IN KNOWLEDGE: Applying a harmonized TR4-5 threshold in ≤ 10 mm nodules reveals substantially differences in classification patterns among the three systems, demonstrating that they are not interchangeable under a uniform risk threshold.

articles.title: Diffusion posterior sampling framework for joint image reconstruction and scatter estimation in cone-beam CT.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: X-ray scatter can have a significant impact on image quality in cone beam CT (CBCT) including the introduction of severe artifacts and CT value inaccuracies. Classic solutions to the scatter problem often involve specialized hardware and data acquisition, or computationally expensive estimation of scatter via Monte Carlo (MC) methods. PURPOSE: We explore a novel scatter correction approach that leverages the recent development of Diffusion Posterior Sampling (DPS) to jointly estimate CT attenuation and scattered radiation directly from single-energy CT projection data. METHODS: We rewrite the nonlinear forward model for CT measurements to include an unknown additive scatter term which we jointly estimate with the image volume. Solution of this ill-posed problem is enabled by diffusion models that capture the distribution of scatter-free images of anatomy. The joint reconstruction and scatter estimation is evaluated using both simulation and phantom data and compared with a MC-based scatter correction method. RESULTS: Qualitative and quantitative results obtained from simulated and phantom data shows that the proposed approach can effectively estimate the scatter contribution, significantly remove scatter artifacts, and restore the overall image contrast and attenuation values. CONCLUSIONS: Joint estimation of scatter and reconstruction for CBCT has the potential to provide improved CBCT image quality and quantitation through direct estimation without the addition of specialized hardware or MC simulations.

articles.title: Rapid coronary computed tomography angiography-derived fractional flow reserve: A feasibility study for on-site assessment.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Fractional flow reserve (FFR) is the reference standard for physiological assessment of coronary artery stenosis severity, but invasive measurement requires catheterization and hyperemic agents. Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived FFR offers a non-invasive alternative, though existing approaches based on computational fluid dynamics (CFD) are computationally intensive and impractical for on-site clinical use. PURPOSE: To evaluate the feasibility of rapidly estimating FFR from CCTA using three mathematical, centerline-based computational methodologies. This study investigates whether pressure-drop formulations relying solely on coronary geometric information can provide rapid FFR estimates suitable for potential on-site clinical application, without the need for computationally intensive fluid dynamics simulations. METHODS: Three CCTA-derived FFR methodologies were evaluated: fixed Fractional Flow Reserve (fFFR3D), mathematical virtual Functional Assessment Index (mvFAI3D), and tomographic Fractional Flow Reserve (tomoFFR). Each method uses the patient mean arterial pressure (MAP) along with the coronary centerline geometry to characterize vessel dimensions and estimate pressure loss under hyperemic conditions. fFFR3D assumes a fixed hyperaemic blood velocity of 0.35 m/s; mvFAI3D extends the virtual Functional Assessment Index (vFAI) using a mathematical pressure-drop formulation; and tomoFFR estimates hyperaemic flow and pressure loss using a baseline fixed-velocity approach. Fourteen coronary vessels from a publicly available dataset with reference invasive FFR measurements were analyzed. Predicted FFR values were compared with clinical measurements (wire measured FFR), with emphasis on classification relative to the clinical threshold of FFR = 0.80  and on computational time. RESULTS: Relative to the FFR = 0.80 threshold, fFFR3D and tomoFFR correctly classified 12 of the 14 vessels (85.7%) and mvFAI3D correctly classified 11 of the 14 vessels (78.6%). Given the limited sample size, no definitive conclusions regarding diagnostic accuracy or generalizability can be drawn. Nevertheless, the results demonstrate the feasibility of applying mathematical pressure-drop models directly to CCTA-derived coronary centerlines. Once centerlines were available, all three approaches required less than 1 s to calculate FFR, enabling substantially faster estimation than conventional CFD-based approaches and supporting potential integration into on-site CCTA analysis workflows. CONCLUSIONS: These findings demonstrate the feasibility of rapid, centerline-based CCTA-derived FFR estimation using mathematical models of coronary pressure loss. Sub-second computational time, combined with the availability of automated AI-based coronary centerline extraction and physician correction in contemporary CCTA workstations, provides a potential pathway toward on-site FFR assessment during routine CT interpretation. Larger prospective, multicenter studies with invasive FFR reference measurements are required to establish diagnostic accuracy, reproducibility, and clinical robustness prior to clinical implementation.

articles.title: Evaluation Design and Model Selection Stability in Medical Image Classification Benchmarks: A Multi-dataset Study.
articles.abstract: Medical image classification benchmarks inform model selection. We assessed how data splits, training seeds, and evaluation conditions affect selection stability and whether repeated evaluation budgets support reproducible rankings. The original study comprised 800 runs on OrganAMNIST and SIPaKMeD, using four ImageNet-initialized convolutional neural networks (CNNs), ten splits, five seeds, and two checkpoint selection and stopping procedures. The 300-run extension evaluated the International Skin Imaging Collaboration (ISIC) 2019 challenge dataset and MURA (musculoskeletal radiographs) using four CNNs, ten splits, and three seeds under procedure A; paired Swin Transformer-Tiny (Swin-T) analyses used five splits and three seeds. Balanced accuracy (BA) defined rankings. Paired resampling quantified selection frequencies and uncertainty; budget analyses compared discovery subsets with held-out splits. Single-context agreement with the full repeated evaluation reference was 44-62% in original strata, 90% for ISIC 2019, and 60% for MURA. The two procedures changed selected identities in 46% of OrganAMNIST and 56% of SIPaKMeD contexts. On matched five-split, three-seed contexts with shared preprocessing, adding Swin-T changed leave-one-split-out agreement from 86.7 to 20.0% in ISIC 2019 and from 66.7 to 80.0% in MURA. At five discovery splits and three seeds, agreement with held-out references ranged from 20.4 to 89.0% in original strata, reaching 100% for ISIC 2019 and 57.1% for MURA. Agreement did not increase uniformly across evaluated budgets. Repeated evaluation revealed both stable and changing selections. Reporting performance alongside selection stability informs budgeting and whether to advance one candidate or retain a shortlist.

articles.title: An Interpretable Multimodal Deep Learning Framework Integrating MRI and Clinical Data via Bidirectional Cross-Modal Attention for Improved Cardiac Disease Detection.
articles.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases continue to be the primary cause of mortality worldwide; however, precise diagnosis is often limited by dependence on individual data modalities and the unclear nature of traditional deep learning models. In this study, we introduce an explainable multimodal deep learning framework that simultaneously analyzes cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and structured clinical variables through a bidirectional cross-modal attention mechanism that operates on token sequences. The architecture utilizes modality-specific encoders ResNet-50 for imaging and a multilayer perceptron for clinical data interconnected through attention that dynamically aligns complementary information, reducing feature dilution and modal dominance. A multitask objective that includes classification, contrastive alignment (InfoNCE), and regularization further reinforces semantic consistency across modalities. Integrated post hoc explainability modules, such as Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping for spatial localization and SHapley Additive exPlanations for clinical feature attribution, offer transparent decision support. Tested on a cohort of 12,847 patients using fivefold cross-validation, the framework achieved an accuracy of 94.2% and an area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve of 0.97, significantly surpassing unimodal and traditional multimodal baselines (p < 0.01). The explanations generated showed 91% concordance with independent cardiologist evaluations. The findings presented herein were derived through internal five-fold cross-validation conducted at a solitary tertiary care institution, thereby substantiating internal validity while limiting multicenter generalizability; consequently, external validation is requisite for broader applicability. These results demonstrate that attention-driven multimodal fusion, combined with post hoc explainability, provides both strong diagnostic performance and clinically useful transparency, positioning the framework as a promising internally validated approach and a foundation for future external validation.

articles.title: Advanced diffusion models in real-world glioma assessment: A comparative analysis of diagnostic performance, pathological correlations, and prognostic value.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Various advanced diffusion models have shown robust diagnostic performance in glioma assessment, yet their relative efficacy has not been comprehensively evaluated. This study aimed to compare continuous-time random walk (CTRW), free water corrected-diffusion tensor imaging (FW-DTI), and mean apparent propagator (MAP) in predicting isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) status and Ki-67 levels of gliomas, investigate their associations with tumor microenvironment (TME) markers, and evaluate their prognostic value in IDH-wildtype patients. METHODS: This retrospective study included 151 patients (83 men; mean age, 47.45 years) with gliomas. CTRW, FW-DTI, MAP, and apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) were processed from diffusion spectrum imaging (DSI), and mean parameter values were extracted. Logistic regression assessed model performance for predicting IDH status and Ki-67 levels. Correlation and Cox regression analyses evaluated their associations with TME markers and prognosis, respectively. RESULTS: CTRW, FW-DTI, MAP, and the combined models showed higher diagnostic performance than ADC, with the combined models achieved the highest numerical AUCs (AUCs 0.930 and 0.859) in identifying IDH status and Ki-67 levels. Except for ADC, no statistically significant differences were observed in diagnostic performance among these models. Additionally, multiple advanced diffusion parameters showed correlations with TME markers, and MAP showed associations with overall survival for IDH-wildtype patients (HR = 4.070, P = 0.020). CONCLUSION: CTRW, FW-DTI, and MAP showed similar predictive performance and outperformed ADC for IDH status and tumor proliferation in gliomas. Their associations with TME markers and the prognostic relevance of MAP support the potential of advanced diffusion imaging for noninvasive pathological and prognostic assessment of gliomas.

articles.title: MRI-derived synthetic [¹⁸F]FET PET in neuro-oncology: evaluation in glioma grading and differentiation from solitary brain metastasis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: O-(2-[18F]fluoroethyl)-L-tyrosine positron emission tomography ([18F]FET PET) is clinically useful in neuro-oncology but limited by cost and availability. We assessed the clinical utility of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-derived synthetic [18F]FET PET. METHODS: A total of 489 patients with histologically confirmed gliomas or brain metastases were retrospectively analyzed. A deep learning model generated synthetic PET images from multimodal MRI in the overall cohort and subgroups. Synthetic PET was evaluated against reference PET for image similarity by peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) and structural similarity index (SSIM), standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) analysis by Pearson correlation and Bland-Altman analysis, and blinded reader assessment for glioma grading and high-grade glioma (HGG) versus solitary brain metastasis (SBM) differentiation using receiver operating characteristic analysis with area under the curve (AUC). RESULTS: Synthetic PET showed high similarity to reference PET in the overall, glioma, and metastasis groups (PSNR, 34.7-35.5 dB; SSIM, 0.90-0.96), and SUVR correlations were strong (r = 0.77-0.93, all P < 0.001), with minimal bias and narrow limits of agreement. Compared with MRI alone, MRI with synthetic PET improved glioma grading and HGG-SBM differentiation, increasing AUC from 0.815 to 0.941 and from 0.816 to 0.901 for glioma grading and from 0.731 to 0.871 and from 0.784 to 0.872 for HGG-SBM differentiation across the 2 readers (all P < 0.05). No significant differences were found between MRI with synthetic and reference PET for either task (all P > 0.05). CONCLUSIONS: MRI-derived synthetic [18F]FET PET may enhance glioma grading and HGG-SBM differentiation, providing a PET-like alternative when FET PET is unavailable.

articles.title: Quantitative evaluation of cervical foraminal stenosis and nerve root diameter using MRI-based multiplanar reconstruction: a prospective study.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Accurate evaluation of cervical foraminal stenosis using conventional MRI is challenging. We quantitatively evaluated cervical foraminal and nerve root diameters using MRI-based multiplanar reconstruction (MPR) and compared measurements between the proximal-type cervical spondylotic amyotrophy (CSA) and cervical spondylotic radiculopathy (CSR) groups. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Twenty-eight consecutive patients were prospectively enrolled: 16 with CSA and C4/5 foraminal stenosis; 12 with CSR without symptomatic C4/5 involvement. T2-weighted coronal MRI was obtained, and images perpendicular to the C4/5 foramen were reconstructed. Foraminal height and anteroposterior diameter, as well as the craniocaudal and anteroposterior diameters of the C5 nerve root, were measured. Side-to-side comparisons were performed in CSA, and measurements were also compared with those in CSR. RESULTS: In CSA, foraminal height was significantly smaller on the symptomatic side than on the asymptomatic side (p = 0.042). The anteroposterior diameters of the C4/5 foramen and C5 nerve root were significantly smaller on the symptomatic side (2.4 ± 0.4 mm vs. 3.1 ± 0.5 mm and 1.9 ± 0.4 mm vs. 2.7 ± 0.5 mm, respectively, p < 0.001). Compared with CSR, the symptomatic side in CSA showed significantly smaller anteroposterior diameters of both the foramen and the nerve root, whereas no significant differences were observed between the asymptomatic side in CSA and CSR. CONCLUSION: MRI-based MPR allows quantitative evaluation of cervical foraminal narrowing and nerve root diameter. Focal anteroposterior narrowing of the C4/5 foramen with reduced diameter of the C5 nerve root was associated with the symptomatic side in CSA.

articles.title: Explainable radiomics and clinical models for prediction of total knee arthroplasty in knee osteoarthritis: data from Osteoarthritis Initiative.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To develop and evaluate MRI radiomics models, with and without clinical variables, for predicting total knee arthroplasty (TKA) within 9 years in patients with knee osteoarthritis. MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective exploratory study included 507 participants from the Osteoarthritis Initiative-Zuse Institute Berlin dataset with manually segmented knee MRIs; 66 underwent TKA. Four hundred radiomics features from bone and cartilage were combined with 13 clinical variables. Logistic regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression, and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were evaluated using radiomics-only, clinical-only, and combined feature sets in an 80/20 development-holdout analysis and stratified nested cross-validation. Preprocessing, feature selection, and tuning were restricted to training folds. RESULTS: On the held-out test set, radiomics-only LASSO had the highest observed AUC-ROC of 0.76 (95% CI, 0.61-0.88), followed closely by combined LASSO at 0.75 (0.61-0.87). Combined logistic regression and XGBoost achieved AUC-ROC values of 0.73 (0.60-0.86) and 0.72 (0.57-0.84), respectively. Differences among the leading models were modest. In nested cross-validation, combined LASSO showed the highest discrimination (AUC-ROC, 0.786 [0.722-0.841]; AUC-PR, 0.343 [0.239-0.451]; F1 score, 0.405 [0.321-0.481]), with modest improvement over radiomics-only LASSO (AUC-ROC, 0.781 [0.717-0.834]). Consistently retained predictors included femoral bone sphericity, femoral cartilage first-order skewness, and WOMAC disability. CONCLUSION: MRI radiomics features, alone or combined with clinical variables, showed potential for predicting TKA risk. Performance differences among leading models were modest, and these exploratory findings require external validation before clinical application.

articles.title: Complications and safety of histotripsy for liver tumours: A narrative review.
articles.abstract: Histotripsy, a non-invasive, non-thermal, cavitation-based ablation technique, received FDA clearance for liver tumours in October 2023, but its safety literature remains limited and its harm profile may differ from thermal ablation. We conducted a narrative review of hepatic histotripsy safety, searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science (2010-June 2026, updated October 2026). Findings were synthesised qualitatively given the small, heterogeneous, largely single-arm evidence base. Procedure-related major complications occurred in 3/44 (7%) pivotal-trial participants. In the post-market cohort, 12/230 (5.2%) patients had complications of any grade, and the three grade > II events were deaths attributed to disease progression. The principal severe-harm signal was vascular: in a single multicentre series, serious pseudoaneurysm/haemorrhage occurred in 4/139 patients (2.9%), three requiring embolisation and one fatal; this is not a pooled incidence. No tumour seeding was identified. Hepatic histotripsy has a low major-complication rate but is not free of serious harm; cavitation-mediated vascular injury is under-represented in pooled literature. Which patients benefit from early post-procedural imaging should be defined prospectively, alongside case-inclusive harm surveillance.

articles.title: Assessment of autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease severity using deep learning-based kidney volumetry in CT.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Accurate quantification of total kidney volume (TKV) and Mayo imaging classification (MIC) is essential for assessing disease severity in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). This study aimed to develop and validate a deep learning-based method using noncontrast computed tomography (CT) scans to automate TKV measurement and MIC assignment. MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective dataset of 60 ADPKD patients was used to train a three-dimensional (3D) UNet model for kidney segmentation and TKV estimation. Kidney axes were calculated using principal component analysis (PCA). The model was tested on consecutive scans from 30 patients (median interval: 3.6 years) and 28 external patient scans. Segmentation accuracy was evaluated using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), and measurement reliability was assessed using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC). MIC was assigned and compared across timepoints. RESULTS: The model achieved high segmentation accuracy (DSC: 0.93 ± 0.04 [mean ± standard deviation] and 0.94 ± 0.03 for consecutive scans; 0.96 ± 0.08 for external validation). Manual and automated TKV measurements were strongly correlated (ICC: 0.94-0.99, p < 0.001), with a mean volume error of 7.61 ± 7.26%. MIC assignment matched in 90-93.3% of cases. Kidney dimensions (length > 16.5 cm, width > 9.5 cm, depth > 8 cm) predicted high-risk MIC classes with positive predictive values > 88%. Longitudinal analysis showed significant increases in TKV and declines in estimated glomerular filtration rate-eGFR (p < 0.001). CONCLUSION: The proposed method enables accurate TKV quantification and MIC classification from noncontrast CT, supporting severity assessment and longitudinal monitoring in ADPKD. KEY POINTS: Question Can a deep learning method using noncontrast CT accurately automate total kidney volume measurement and Mayo Imaging Classification assignment in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease? Findings In internal and external testing, automated kidney segmentation showed high agreement with reference measurements and correctly assigned Mayo Imaging Classification in most cases with overall accuracy. Relevance statement Automated analysis of noncontrast CT provided reliable kidney volume quantification and disease severity classification, reducing manual workload while enabling longitudinal assessment of disease progression in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease.

articles.title: Ultrasound-guided marker placement and blue dye staining for sentinel lymph node biopsy in early-stage breast cancer.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Ultrasound (US)-guided marker placement is an emerging method for sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB), and this study aimed to investigate the concordance between US-guided marker placement for peri-foraminal lymph nodes (LNs) in the axillary cribriform fascia and blue dye-stained SLNs, especially the utility of the two concurrent labeling methods for SLNB in patients with early-stage breast cancer. METHODS: Female patients with clinically staged T1-2N0M0 breast cancer were enrolled. Patients received US-guided marker placement on the day before surgery, followed by blue dye staining. SLN biopsy was performed on the blue dye-stained LNs first and then on the US-guided markers. RESULTS: A total of 96 eligible patients were enrolled. The detection rates of US-guided localization, blue dye, and their combination were 100.0%, 95.8%, and 100.0%, respectively. Among the 92 patients with blue dye staining, US-guided markers were found in blue-stained LNs from 91 patients (concordant) but failed in 1 patient (non-concordant); among the 4 patients without blue-stained LNs. US-guided markers were found in all 4 patients (non-concordant), resulting in a general concordance rate of 94.8% (91/96). Notably, among the 92 patients with blue dye staining, 23 had LN metastasis diagnosed through SLNB, whereas among the 4 patients without blue-stained LNs, the SLNB was performed based on US-guided markers, which revealed 3 patients with LN metastasis and 1 without. Moreover, combining the two labeling methods concurrently identified 26 patients with LN metastasis. CONCLUSION: US-guided localization combined with blue dye concurrently may be a satisfied option for SLNB detection. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: US-guided localization combined with blue dye offers an accessible, anatomically grounded, and radiation-free strategy for optimizing the SLNB procedure, especially in settings where radioactive isotopes are not available.

Prompt-dependent readability and accuracy of Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 thinking responses to breast imaging questions derived from European Society of Breast Imaging patient recommendations.
articles.abstract: PURPOSE: Although professional societies provide standardized resources, the reliability of online health content remains inconsistent, particularly as large language models (LLMs) become a growing source of patient information. Therefore, the primary objective of this study was to determine whether patient-focused prompt optimization improves the readability of Generative Pre-trained Transformer-5 (GPT-5) Thinking responses compared with standard prompting while evaluating potential changes in expert-rated factual accuracy using educational materials published by the European Society of Breast Imaging (EUSOBI). METHODS: All GPT-5 Thinking outputs were prospectively generated in January 2026. The dataset included frequently asked questions (FAQs) and special information notes (SINs) derived from EUSOBI articles, each submitted under two distinct prompts (standard-Prompt 1 vs. patient-focused-Prompt 2). Readability was quantified using four indices with an averaged composite "reading grade level." Accuracy was scored by two radiologists using a 5-point Likert scale. RESULTS: A total of 48 questions (15 FAQs and 33 SIN-derived questions) were each answered under two prompt conditions, yielding 96 responses for analysis. Prompt 2 produced significantly lower readability levels than Prompt 1 across all indices (P < 0.001). These improvements occurred without significant differences in word count (P = 0.12) or sentence count (P = 0.63). The mean accuracy scores remained high and comparable between prompts for all questions (4.54 ± 0.63 vs. 4.52 ± 0.59, P = 0.75). The inter-rater agreement was almost perfect for both the FAQ and SIN-derived question sets (κ = 0.82 and 0.81, respectively). CONCLUSION: Patient-focused prompting substantially reduced the linguistic complexity and reading grade level of GPT-5 Thinking responses without a statistically significant reduction in expert-rated accuracy, demonstrating its ability to produce more accessible breast imaging content, although the resulting grade level remained above widely recommended patient-education thresholds. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: A simple, low-cost prompt modification can substantially improve the readability of LLM-generated patient education content in breast imaging without a measurable reduction in expert-rated accuracy, although further work is needed to confirm this translates into improved patient comprehension.
